The Opus Cirro Is a Lightweight, Self-Inflating Camper With a King Bed
24 photos
Photo: Opus Camper
Life is all about compromises, choices, and priorities, though not necessarily in that order. The Opus Cirro hybrid camper would like to take some compromises out of the equation, while making the choice easier for future RV-ers.
Opus Cirro is the latest offering from UK-based Opus Camper , a company that maintains a strong presence on the international stage, including partners in Europe, the U.S., and Australia. It's also the smallest and lightest offer from that catalog, which in itself is notable, seeing how they specialize in lightweight and compact solutions.
Opus Camper does hybrid campers – towables that travel tiny and then expand into home-like habitats at camp with the help of canvas extensions. What makes these hybrid trailers different from other hybrids from the same niche is the fact that Opus uses a patented Air System to have them self-inflate. It's all fun and no work for you once you've opened their clamshell-like base, is what this means.
All this trickles down to the Opus Cirro, the newest member of the self-inflating camper family. First teased at the 2026 Dusseldorf Caravan Salon and then at the 2026 NEC Caravan in Birmingham the following month, the Cirro is ready for its big, formal debut.
Photo: Opus Camper The new model isn't yet available, but the pre-order books are finally open. Last time we looked at it, buzz online claimed that Opus was eyeing an early 2027 delivery date, which seems to be confirmed in the video tour at the bottom of the page. It will be just in time for the new summer camping season.
The Cirro targets a very specific type of customer, which will go a long way to explain why it's so basic in terms of equipment. It's designed for the occasional camper who drives either an electric vehicle (EV) or a compact car, and who maybe is upgrading from a traditional tent.
It's a basic, stripped-down version of the bigger models Opus offers, but in return, it offers to that camper the possibility to bring along two more family members or even as many as six if they add extra kit, to choose their own gear in terms of cooking and bathroom facilities, and a high degree of garageability.
Photo: Opus Camper This hybrid camper might not offer much in terms of actual comfort beyond the perk of sleeping off the ground, under a nice shelter, but it does have several pros – a light weight and compact form factor being among them.
On the road, the Cirro is a hair over 3.5 meters (11.4 feet) long from tip of the drawbar to the rear and just 1.8 meters (5.9 feet) wide. It rides on a single-axle chassis that can be ordered braked or unbraked, and presents – in road mode – as a shell of insulated aluminum panels. Opus themselves describe it as "super-cute and dinky," which is true. It's also perfect for a standard garage and will tow with ease.
Empty weight is just 500 kg (1,102 lbs), while maximum permissible weight is 750 kg (1,653 lbs). You can add a pair of optional racks on the lid of the clamshell to carry up to 75 kg (165 lbs) of cargo there, whether kayaks or storage boxes.
Photo: Opus Camper At camp, you open the lid of the trailer and plop it on sturdy support legs. That area will become the suspended base of the bedroom, which comes with tent liners, an LED sleeve, opening windows with screen mesh, and most importantly, a bed that's bigger than a standard king.
The upper section is tent canvas, though not the one Opus uses for their bigger models. This one is technical cotton fabric that promises to be waterproof, durable, and breathable, and it inflates by means of two pumps powered by twin 3000mAh OPUS Blow Bank batteries built directly into the air tube structure. The batteries are removable for charging and the entire system is protected from the elements.
Bigger Opus campers boast installation as fast as a couple of minutes. The Cirro takes a bit more, even though it's smaller, because the Air System itself is stripped down. Opus says complete setup at camp takes "under 10 minutes," which is still decent if you consider it's zero effort on your part.
Photo: Opus Camper With the structure in place, you get a camper that's 4.6 meters (15 feet) long and 2 meters (6.5 feet) high inside, with a sense of space you probably won't find in similar products. The Cirro comes with several large windows throughout and two skylights, one more LED sleeve in the living space, and a seating area comprised of a longer bench that extends into a single bed and a small bench.
Tucked in a dedicated storage compartment at the front is a removable, foldable table that will fit inside on rainy days. Open cubbies for storage are included under the longer bench, as are USB-A and USB-C outlets. At camp, the Cirro hooks up to the mains with a 230V connection.
Opus says that the Cirro can be optioned with a Comfort Package that adds custom graphite alloy wheels, a large 180-liter (6.3 cu-ft) metal storage box on the tongue, a 35-liter (1.2 cu-ft) compressor fridge, a spare tire with carrier mounted underneath, sideskirts, a windbreak kit, and upgraded upholstery in a suede-like fabric.
Photo: Opus Camper They also highlight compatibility with the older Air Sun canopy or the full awning kit, which adds more living space that you can use either for fitting more beds (up to four) or a kitchen. These will also add to the final price, but pre-ordering a bundle will supposedly save you a lot of cash.
Since we're on the topic, the base Cirro is priced at around around £13,500, which would be approximately €16,100 or $17,900 at the current exchange rate. The Cirro Comfort Package is obviously more expensive, at around £15,000 (€18,000/$19,800).

Pentagon grapples with growth of artificial intelligence. (Graphic by Breaking Defense, original brain graphic via Getty)
WASHINGTON — The Defense Department announced today that it has redesignated its Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office ( CDAO ) as the Super Intelligence Office (SIO).
The DoD said the new name does not reflect a change in mission but rather aligns the office’s designation with the Trump administration’s broader effort to replace references to artificial intelligence with “super intelligence” across the federal government. Cameron Stanley, the department’s top AI official who also helms the SIO, said in a statement that the rebrand also reflects the Pentagon’s priorities moving forward.
“We have moved beyond experimental prototypes. As the Super Intelligence Office, our mission is to harness the full power of sovereign Super Intelligence to ensure decisive military superiority across every domain,” Stanley said.
The redesignation follows President Donald Trump’s September announcement that all federal agencies should replace references to AI with the term super intelligence, or SI. At the time, he argued that the word “artificial” made the technology sound fake, despite its growing capabilities.
The terminology shift has raised questions within the tech community, where “superintelligence” has historically referred to a specific , hypothetical form of general artificial intelligence that exceeds overall human intelligence — a capability that does not currently exist.
The Pentagon has been among the federal government’s most aggressive adopters of AI technology, with the CDAO leading efforts to expand its use across military operations and department functions. Those efforts include making artificial intelligence tools more widely available to military personnel through GenAI.mil an enterprise platform providing users access to commercial generative AI models.
The office’s portfolio includes the Maven Smart System , an AI-enabled intelligence and targeting platform, and the War Data Platform, a central data hub formerly known as Advana . The CDAO has also spearheaded numerous exercises and experimentation efforts aimed at integrating artificial intelligence and other advanced capabilities across the department.
The CDAO’s transition to SIO “will roll out across digital systems, enterprise applications and component headquarters over the coming weeks,” the DoD said. “Existing operational programs, industry solicitations and defense partnerships will continue uninterrupted under the new banner.” The department has also launched SI.mil , which will serve as the renamed office’s primary digital domain.

The U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE) Advanced Research Projects Agency-Energy (ARPA-E) has selected eight projects that could receive up to a combined $30 million to accelerate development of geothermal technologies. The funding announced November 12 is through the Stimulate Utilization of Plentiful Energy in Rocks through High-temperature Original Technologies (SUPERHOT) program. The projects will develop innovative approaches to harness superhot geothermal resources at temperatures above 375C and pressures above 22 megapascals to expand access to reliable baseload power.
“SUPERHOT pursues exponential, not incremental, progress by pushing the boundaries of innovation to fundamentally change how we tap into geothermal energy,” said ARPA-E Director Conner Prochaska. “The Energy Department is investing in technologies that could unlock America’s vast untapped energy potential and increase geothermal well productivity to deliver affordable, reliable, and secure power to American families and businesses.”
The U.S. holds at least 15,000 GW of potential geothermal power beneath its surface, yet existing technologies currently generate less than 4 GW of utility-scale power. Building on ARPA-E’s work to advance Enhanced Geothermal Systems (EGS) and Advanced Geothermal Systems (AGS), SUPERHOT aims to more than triple the output of individual geothermal wells by overcoming challenges in well construction and heat transfer. These advancements could help meet growing U.S. energy demand by delivering 10–20 GW of baseload power at less than $30 per megawatt-hour by 2040.
Selected projects include those led by the University of Oklahoma (Norman, OK); Oak Ridge National Laboratory (Oak Ridge, TN); Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (Livermore, CA); XGS Energy (Houston, TX); Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (Richland, WA); the University of Southern California (Los Angeles, CA); Los Alamos National Laboratory (Los Alamos, NM); and Blade Energy Partners, Ltd. (Houston, TX).
Learn more about the selected projects here and the SUPERHOT program here .

Man Pulls Off Heist, Buys Used 2024 Chevrolet Corvette E-Ray Coupe 3LZ ZER for $38,300 Under MSRP
27 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer/autoevolution
Man, do I like this E-Ray! It's not a top-spec car, but it's not lightly optioned either, and for $87,500 with 3,200 miles on the clock, this is a genuine steal. Maybe it could have done with some additional exterior carbon fiber aero bits, the highly expensive carbon fiber wheels or the Competition Sport bucket seats (if that's your preference), but at the end of the day, this is still a 3LZ ZER. As far as I'm concerned, it's got everything you need.
This settles it. I've come around to the E-Ray big time. They're starting to become cheaper, on average, than the Z06, and buyers are answering the call. We can talk about how superior the Grand Sport X is all day long (not to mention the ZR1X), but at the end of the day, most people just want to drive home after having struck a good deal - and they don't get much better than this.
So, this car retailed for $125,860 originally, and whoever bought it now (at auction) just paid nearly $40,000 under MSRP. Plus a buyer's fee, to be fair. Regardless, this might be the cheapest E-Ray we've ever seen and you're buying so much car for the money, it's crazy.
I know it doesn't have the enthusiast appeal of the Z06 with its high-revving flat plane crank V8, but the end-result is more or less the same when it comes to straight line performance. The Z06's 5.5-liter LT6 V8 is pushing down 670 hp while revving to 8,600 rpm, whereas the E-Ray boasts the same 6.2-liter LT2 V8 you'd find in the Stingray, albeit with a 160-horsepower electric motor at the front, for a total of 655 hp. It'll only rev to 6,600 rpm.
But it's got all-wheel drive, and you can drive it on electric power alone, and that's definitely worth certain considerations.
Aside from its Riptide Blue Metallic exterior, this E-Ray also comes with Carbon Flash accents, LED headlights, plus a set of Carbon Flash-finished 20" and 21" forged wheels rocking Michelin Pilot Sport 4S rubber and Edge Red-finished calipers over carbon-ceramic discs. There's also a front-axle lift system, while the seller added the Carbon Flash front splitter, a wicker bill rear spoiler extension, splash guards, and over-the-top-stripes.
Photo: Bring a Trailer Personally, I'd be perfectly comfortable removing the stripes, and maybe wrapping the car a different color - I'm not the biggest Riptide Blue Metallic fan. But to each their own.
Meanwhile, interior highlights include the heated and ventilated GT2 bucket seats in Jet Black Napa leather with Adrenaline Red contrast stitching, Torch Red seat belts, dual-zone automatic climate control, cruise control, a 10-speaker Bose sound system, head-up display, and a heated and leather-trimmed steering wheel.
As for performance, we already touched on that a little bit. I will add that in a straight line, the E-Ray can hit 60 mph (97 kph) in 2.5 seconds (with a 1-foot rollout), before maxing out at 184 mph (296 kph).

Electric truck operator Nevoya is expanding its deal with Meta with the fresh deployment of 25 Class 8 battery-electric trucks on the Interstate 10 (I-10) between San Bernardino, California and Phoenix, Arizona … but Meta won’t be shipping any products.
The second major trucking deal between Facebook parent company Meta and electric truck operator Nevoya will put 25 new battery-electric semis on I-10, running freight between San Bernardino, California and Phoenix, Arizona . But Meta isn’t buying trucks, hiring drivers or shipping its own products. Instead, Zuck’s company helping pay for someone else’s cleaner freight through environmental attribute certificates (EACs), a carbon credit mechanism that lets companies claim the emissions benefits of electric trucking without operating the trucks themselves.
“Coming back to Nevoya for a second corridor reflects what we look for in our value chain work: partners that can scale, and agreements we can repeat, said Devon Lake, Head of Net Zero Strategy, Meta. “Freight is part of the emissions footprint of building and operating our data centers, and multi-year commitments like this help address our scope 3 emissions and make electric trucking available and competitive on the routes that serve the regions where we build.”
Meta was one of several buyers in the DC-based Center for Green Market Activation (GMA) buyers’ alliance. The group’s collective EAC purchases supported Nevoya’s initial 63-truck deployment on the Houston–Dallas corridor back in May . This new Agreement, however, is a standalone deal between Nevoya and Meta only, and gives Meta an established framework to open more electric truck corridors in the future.

This clever application of these agreements is what makes the Dallas-Houston run stand out, with GMA calling it, “the first large-scale application of book and claim to zero-emission trucking.” The company adds that this arrangement helps client companies overcome existing barriers to EV adoption while enabling Nevoya to deploy new trucks, “where they deliver the strongest commercial and operational value.”
Nevoya expects Meta’s fresh batch of semis to begin prowling I-10 in 2027, where they’ll cover approximately 4 million freight miles annually.

View of the Manantial Espejo processing plant. Credit: Santa Cruz government.
By: Northern Miner Staff November 13, 2026
Cerrado Gold (TSXV: CERT) acquired Pan American Silver’s (TSX, NYSE: PAAS) idled Manantial Espejo gold-silver operation in Argentina for $20 million (C$28.5 million), targeting a return to production in 2027. The stock rose.
The acquisition, announced Friday , includes a 2,500-tonne-per-day mill in Santa Cruz province. Cerrado paid $10 million upfront, with two $5-million instalments due on the first and second anniversaries of closing. Pan American receives a 1% net smelter return royalty on all future production to settle intercompany debt.
Cerrado bought all shares of Minera Tritón Argentina, the mine’s owner. Its Minera Don Nicolás subsidiary will fund the purchase and restart. Some concessions also carry a pre-existing 0.5% net smelter return royalty.
“With funds available in Argentina to support our development plans, we believe this opportunity should enhance shareholder value without shareholder dilution,” Cerrado CEO Mark Brennan said Friday.
Cerrado shares climbed 5% to C$2.23 Friday morning in Toronto, valuing the company at about C$318 million ($224 million). The stock has ranged between C$1.31 and C$2.83 in the past year.
Provincial footprint
The purchase expands Cerrado’s presence in Santa Cruz, where it operates Minera Don Nicolás. Existing infrastructure offers a route back to production, but refurbishment and an economic supply of mill feed remain essential. Cerrado hasn’t provided a restart budget or production targets.
The buyer assumes historical, current and future liabilities, including closure obligations and a required $13.8-million financial guarantee.
Certain permits will require updating or renewal before mining resumes. Mining ended in late 2022, with residual processing completed in January 2023.
Refurbishment first
The mine lies about 160 km west of Puerto San Julián. Dewatering and refurbishment could take up to six months, with initial mill throughput targeted at 1,000 tonnes daily. Cerrado plans to process low-grade stockpiles first, then blend in newly mined underground material.
About 40,000 metres of drilling are planned in 2027 to support an initial resource estimate, Cerrado said. Restarting without a feasibility study based on reserves carries a higher risk of technical or economic failure, the company cautioned.
Santa Cruz’s provincial government welcomed the ownership change on Friday, identifying rehabilitation, dewatering and equipment repairs as the first tasks. Exploration and geological evaluation would proceed alongside that work, the government said.
Governor Claudio Vidal’s administration has made recovering the operation a provincial objective, tying the proposed restart to employment and local investment. Its statement described a recovery program leading towards a future reopening, without announcing a production date or output target.
Rising output
The acquisition comes amid improving output at Cerrado’s existing Argentine operations. Minera Don Nicolás produced 16,685 gold-equivalent oz. in the third quarter, 21% more than a year earlier, bringing nine-month output to 44,942 gold-equivalent oz., Cerrado said in its October operating update.
Cerrado then expected full-year production near the upper end of its 50,000 to 60,000 gold-equivalent-oz. target range. Exploration at the recently acquired Falcon and Calandrias II properties is intended to support a new preliminary economic assessment for Minera Don Nicolás by late March.
The existing operation has both carbon-in-leach and heap-leach processing, allowing it to treat material of different grades. Cerrado has made regional acquisitions part of its strategy to expand that resource base and extend operating life.

The rate of pay growth was tied for eighth of 10 sectors tracked. Credit: Amanda Stutt.
Posted By: Frik Els November 13, 2026
Canada’s mining and oil and gas workers have the country’s highest average weekly earnings by a wide margin. They are also, this fall, among the worst-rewarded for staying loyal.
New payroll data from ADP Canada , drawn from the paycheques of roughly 1.6 million private-sector workers, show median gross pay growth for workers who stayed in their jobs in natural resources and mining was 4.1% year over year in October.
The rate of pay growth was unchanged from September and tied for eighth of the 10 sectors ADP tracks. It also came in below the national figure of 4.5% for job-stayers. Only “other services” (3.3%), which includes everyone from barbers to pastors, did worse.
The sector sharing eighth place with mining and the oil patch is information, the closest thing in the data to tech (but it also includes journalists). Tech may be feeling the first effects of growing AI use especially for junior positions, but finance, which also looks ripe for superintelligence disruption, fared much better, at 5%.
Statistics Canada’s payroll survey, which lags the ADP data by two months, puts average weekly earnings in mining, quarrying and oil and gas at $2,584 in August, against $1,355 across all industries and $531 in accommodation and food services. A 5.4% raise on $531 is about $29 a week and 4.1% on $2,584 is about $106.
StatCan also shows slower growth in average weekly earnings in the combined mining, quarrying and oil and gas sector – up only 0.8% year over year. The all-industry figure rose 3.7%.
Naturally volatile
ADP’s natural resources (mainly oil and gas and a few farmworkers and loggers) and mining category has been the most volatile pay sector in the country since January 2023. It is roughly four times as volatile as manufacturing as measured by the standard deviation of its monthly pay-growth readings. In July 2023, workers in the sector recorded gross pay growth of nearly 12%.
The sector held the top spot for eight straight months. By March 2026, the same series had sunk to 2.9%, the lowest of any sector, where it stayed for five months. Manufacturing’s range over that period is no more than 2.4 percentage points while mining’s swings and roundabouts come to 8.6 percentage points. A quick glance at NYMEX or COMEX will explain why.
Onus on bonus
Base pay – the hourly rate or salary, stripped of overtime, bonuses and commissions – for natural resources and mining job-stayers is growing at 3%. Growth is similar in every other sector: all 10 are at 3% or 3.1%. Canadian consumer prices rose about 10% over 2022 and 2023 combined.
Canada’s most recent inflation rate was 3.1% in October, but in September gasoline was 28% and airfares 19% more expensive than a year earlier. StatCan says alcohol, tobacco and cannabis are only 1.6% dearer.
It’s often boom and bust in mining and gross pay follows the up and down cycles. In October 2023, the sector’s gross pay growth (11%) outran its base pay growth (4.5%) by 6.5 percentage points, a gap between the two growth rates no other sector came close to. In October 2026, the gap is 1.1 percentage points, and it has turned negative three times in two years, most recently in March.
FIFO FOMO
Compounding ADP’s October median pay-growth readings from 2023 through 2026 produces an illustrative increase of about 27% for natural resources and mining, compared with 22% nationally. The sector leads the comparison, just ahead of financial activities and leisure and hospitality. These calculations combine annual snapshots; they do not measure the cumulative gains of individual workers.
Loyalty: for dogs
ADP doesn’t break out job-hopping by sector. Nationally, job-changers saw gross pay rise 10% in October against 4.5% for stayers, a gap of 5.9 percentage points using unrounded figures, the widest since February 2024 and more than three percentage points wider than a year ago, when switchers’ raises bottomed at 7.1%. Base pay tells the same story: 6% for changers, 3% for stayers.
If the market is paying job-changers 10%, the arithmetic of staying put looks like a grind, particularly for mid-career workers. Among job-stayers across the economy, those aged 35 to 54 saw gross pay rise 4.4% in October, close to the national figure. Those aged 55 and older got 2.9%. Only stayers under 25, at 11%, kept pace with switchers, and that is the usual early-career ramp.
There is good news. The combined mining and oil and gas sector has added jobs over the past year. StatCan’s payroll count for mining, quarrying and oil and gas extraction rose 3.9% year over year in August to 226,600, the fastest growth of any of the 20 sectors it tracks, in an economy where overall payroll employment grew only 0.3%.

Tesla has pulled the $41,990 Model Y All-Wheel Drive from its US online configurator. The cheapest dual-motor Model Y you can order now is the Model Y Premium AWD at $49,990, an $8,000 jump.
The trim lasted just over nine months. Tesla launched it in early February, and it’s gone without a word from the company.
What’s left in the Model Y lineup
Here’s what Tesla’s US Model Y design studio lists as of today (prices before the destination fee):
Model Y Rear-Wheel Drive: $39,990 (348 miles EPA, 0-60 mph in 6.8 seconds)
Model Y Premium Rear-Wheel Drive: $45,990 (355 miles, 5.4 seconds)
Model Y Premium All-Wheel Drive: $49,990 (327 miles, 4.3 seconds)
Model Y Performance: $57,990
Model Y L Premium (six seats): $61,990
Tesla’s US Model Y configurator on November 13, 2026. The only AWD options left start at $49,990. (Source: Tesla)
When Tesla launched the base Model Y AWD in February , it was basically the stripped-down Model Y with a second motor. It had 294 miles of range, did 0-60 mph in 4.6 seconds and kept the same cut-down cabin as the base RWD. At a $2,000 premium over the single-motor version, it was the most sensible AWD pricing Tesla had offered in years.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
And the AWD trim isn’t the only change. In February, the Premium RWD cost $44,990 and the Premium AWD cost $48,990. Both are now $1,000 higher.
Add it up and the cheapest all-wheel-drive Model Y went from $41,990 to $49,990 in nine months. That’s a 19% increase.
Rivals still sell AWD crossovers for about $40,000
The timing isn’t great for Tesla’s competitive position. Chevrolet’s 2027 Equinox EV LT 1 AWD starts at $40,295 before destination, with 307 miles of EPA range. Ford’s Mustang Mach-E Select AWD starts at $40,795.
Both now undercut Tesla’s cheapest AWD crossover by more than $9,000.
If you live somewhere it snows and you were shopping for a new Model Y, the math just got a lot worse. You can still find some base AWD units in Tesla’s inventory, but once those are gone, that’s it.
This is also the latest cut in a year of Tesla shrinking its lineup. Elon Musk killed the Model S and Model X in January to free up Fremont for Optimus, and Cybertruck production is winding down. Meanwhile, the most recent new Tesla is the $61,990 Model Y L , which sits at the top of the range, not the bottom.
Electrek’s Take
We liked this trim. It was the first time in a long time that Tesla treated all-wheel drive as a $2,000 option rather than a huge upsell bundled with a nicer interior, and it put the Model Y right in the price bracket of the Equinox EV and Mach-E with AWD.
Now it’s gone, and the Premium trims went up $1,000 on top of that. Tesla didn’t explain either move. It rarely does anymore.
There are two plausible reasons. Either Tesla is tight on Model Y build slots and would rather fill them with higher-margin Premium trims, or the cheap AWD simply wasn’t selling. We don’t know which. But both explanations land in the same place for buyers: a more expensive Model Y.
And Tesla has a habit of this. The “Standard” name for its cheaper Model Y and Model 3 lasted a few months. The single-motor Cybertruck, the only version that made sense, was gone within days. Cheaper trims show up, get a news cycle, and quietly disappear.
That’s a problem for a company whose consumer lineup is shrinking down to two cars. The Model Y is Tesla’s volume. Thinning it out at the bottom is the opposite of what you’d do if growing EV sales were the priority.
How long before the $39,990 RWD goes the same way?

Engwe has impressed us repeatedly with its value e-bikes at l ower-than-believable prices . But lately, the brand is climbing the value chain with impressive e-bikes that aren’t just great value but also pack strong specs and impressive features . The Engwe M20 3.0 is a great example…
The Engwe M20 3.0 is a specs monster and blows away the original version of the bike released in 2023 :
40 mph: Top speed in unlocked off-road mode, hitting 0–15 mph in 2.15 seconds. With heavier riders, expect a few mph less
120 Nm: Peak torque output from the 750W-rated (3300W peak) rear hub motor. You read that right. They are saying a 3.3kW motor is rated at the legal 750W. Why not at this point? Everything is 750W!
180 miles: Maximum claimed pedal-assist range with the dual 60V 20Ah (2,400Wh) battery setup, dropping to roughly 85 miles on throttle alone. I rode about 40 miles for this review, and the battery just lost 1 bar.
2 hours: Time to charge a single battery from 0% to 80% using the included 8A fast charger. A little math tells us the full story. 60V*8A = 480W. 480Wx2 hours = 960Wh. You still have another half hour of charging to get the the full 1.2kWh.
102 lbs: Total curb weight, paired with a 330-pound maximum payload capacity. Heavier riders will push that to the limit if they have passengers.
$1,399–$1,699: Typical retail pricing depending on battery configuration and current sales. We have 10% off code ELECTREKCO which brings it all the way down to $1259
The M20 is fairly easy to assemble. At just over 100lbs, it is a bit hard to move around, but once assembled, it feels like a pretty impressive piece of machinery. I love the street tires on here instead of pretending to be an off-roader. Dual bright headlights and brake light with turn signals really give this thing some street cred. Adding to the safety roster, Engwe upgraded the quad-piston brakes with sporty red calipers and 202 mm rotors. This is not a value bike. The rear suspension is tight, which is great for 2 riders but might feel stiff out of the box for light riders. The seat is *chef’s kiss* even for 2 riders. Very soft and comfortable but not too soft. It even has a little ‘gas tank’ storage area aft the seat, which is keyed and enough to hold a few sandwiches, some riding gloves, or a small purse.
One gripe: There are 3 sets of keys on here, the aforementioned storage area and one set each for each battery. We’d love to see these things keyed together.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The bike/moped/moto came with a huge 1.2 kW battery (or 2 in our case – unless you have a 80-mile commute, 1 should be plenty) that must be charged individually. But with a 60V 8A charger, each one only takes about 2-3 hours to charge, which is impressive.
The Engwe M20 ride
I did not expect to like the ride of this thing as much as I did. We can dispense with the pleasantries here; it came set to Class 2 mode with a 20mph top speed and stickers to match; a quick Google search will show you how to open this up to 40mph open mode. I take responsibility for my own actions.
The first thing you’ll notice here is that the motor is whisper-quiet, and with the street tires, there is very little road noise, even at 35mph. The half throttle is plenty responsive, a lot more so than the cadence sensor on the pedals, which are vestigial at best here. Those big brakes are a bit softer than I’d prefer, but given a good squeeze, those 203mm rotors and quad-piston hydraulic brakes are going to stop you, the 100lb bike, and your passenger/cargo fairly quickly.
The cops
My girlfriend and I got pulled over for the first time in my e-biking life as I was picking her up at the coffee shop. The cop was immediately apologetic because “he thought we were kids” and not the 50-year-olds under the helmets he encountered. Then he noticed the pedals and said that we’re all clear and that what we were on looked like a motorcycle and that a couple of e-moto kids had gotten into accidents recently, one hit by a drunk driver and who is still in a coma. While he was already letting us go, I pointed out the Class 2 sticker on the bike, and he gave me the thumbs-up as we sped off at 30mph. This M20 passed the local police test with flying colors. I can’t guarantee you’ll have the same experience in your jurisdiction.
M20 Downsides
Most of my gripes on this e-bike are inherent to the form factor. It is heavy at over 100 lbs, but you’d expect that with a 3.3kW motor, 2.4kW of batteries, and room for two. That said, don’t buy this bike if you need to take it up stairs or plan to pedal it without assist. In fact, this isn’t a bikepath bike or a put it on the back of your car bike. And, don’t buy this bike if you like to pedal. It’s too big and fast. This is a 35 mph roads bike. Also 3 sets of keys?
Electrek’s take:
I did not expect to love this bike as much as I have. It is the perfect train station bike for me, and as a bonus, it is a great way to take my girlfriend to the coffee shop on the weekends. It has fat tires, great suspension, a cushy seat, and strong, smooth acceleration and confidence-inspiring braking. It looks cool enough for the cops to think I’m a kid picking up his girlfriend, and it has so much range that I probably won’t need to charge it monthly. At $1399-$1699 ( 10% off ) depending on battery config, this is less than half the price of some of the pricier and admittedly more stylish Super73 options out there.
I understand that some will fault Engwe for selling a 3.3kW motor e-bike as a class 2 e-bike. But I genuinely feel safer on the road, being able to go at the 35mph speed that cars are going rather than forcing them to go around me. Plus, it isn’t like every single car on the road goes over the speed limit. So why not bikes too?
The Engwe M20 3.0 is over the limit but in all of the best possible ways.

The Airelume 260 Is a Different Kind of Family Travel Trailer, Sleeps Nine Without Slide-Outs
17 photos
Photo: Forest River/ That RV Girl
An old adage says there is beauty in simplicity, and this is valid for many aspects of life. The saying applies even to the RV life, where stripping away excess weight, complicated systems, unnecessary ornamentation, and clutter creates space for more freedom and adventure.
Introduced earlier in 2026 in partnership with dealer Camping World, Forest River’s Airelume range of travel trailers follows precisely this philosophy. Instead of chasing trends and fitting their RVs with features that might end up unused, the company focused on creating a lineup that includes features that campers actually use and that “make everyday camping moments easier and more enjoyable.”
Inspired by customer feedback and designed with intention, the Airelume range aims to strike a balance between quality construction, practical design, and reasonable pricing. In the short time since its introduction, the lineup has already expanded to include 13 floor plans that vary widely in size and configuration, so there is a model for everyone, from solo travelers and couples to large families.
The Airelume 260 is a travel trailer aimed at families or groups of friends with a bunkhouse floor plan that manages to accommodate up to nine people while keeping its weight below 6,400 pounds (2,900 kg). It measures just under 29 feet (8.8 meters) in length and is characterized by refreshing simplicity and practicality.
Photo: Forest River/ That RV Girl While most family-oriented RVs resort to slide-outs or lofts to expand the available square footage and sleeping capacity, the Airelume 260 offers double bunks, a queen bed, and convertible sleeping areas, alongside a kitchen, dinette, and bathroom, in a zero-slideout design. But what makes it even more appealing is that it still offers a residential feel, with practical amenities and details such as a dedicated coffee nook, a sofa built for real legroom, industry-leading countertop, a 60K water heater, and more.
It is a dual-axle travel trailer with a single entrance, and like all the models in the Airelume lineup, it boasts a powder-coated I-beam frame, a Tufflex PVC roof, and an enclosed underbelly. On the outside, it showcases a catchy white and blue color scheme with color-matched fenders and the Airelume badge on the front cap.
The exterior equipment is kept simple and functional, with a pass-through storage compartment at the front, manual stabilizers and a manual tongue jack, accessible propane tanks, and a dedicated battery compartment. There is also a bumper-mounted spare tire at the rear, as well as preparation for an observation camera. The side of the trailer houses the main utility connections and a black tank flush.
Photo: Forest River/ That RV Girl One of the Airelume 260’s strongest suits is the generous sleeping capacity it manages to offer within a relatively compact footprint . As already mentioned, it can accommodate up to nine people without making the interior feel claustrophobic or hard to navigate for daily activities.
Many travel trailers with similar sleeping capacity rely on slide-outs or have a longer body, but this model manages to do it with a clever interior arrangement: a front queen bedroom, a rear bunk area that offers a double-over-double setup, a jackknife sofa that pulls into a bed, and a convertible dinette.
The bunkhouse boasts a clever notched design, just like we’ve seen on the Airelume 265 floor plan , allowing for two spacious sleeping levels, each with lighting and its own window. There’s also storage beneath the bunks and roof vent above that helps with air circulation.
At the other end of the trailer, the main bedroom is a more conventional sleeping space with a walk-around queen bed flanked by windows with privacy shades, bedside shelves, a wardrobe, and some deep cubbies for additional closet space. There is also under-bed storage and interior access to the front pass-through compartment.
Photo: Forest River/ That RV Girl The only caveat regarding this arrangements is the lack of privacy. There are no full walls and solid doors to separate the central common living area of the trailer from the rear and front sleeping spaces. However, for the main bedroom, there is a partial wall that creates a sense of separation and owners can later add a curtain for some privacy.
The single-block kitchen is located on the campsite and comes with some features meant to make the compact space more convenient to use. I’m referring, of course, to the dedicated Coffee Corner with K-Cup holder, cubbies for storing supplies, hooks for hanging cups, and an electrical outlet for a coffee maker. There is even an overhead microwave in this area.
The kitchen is also fully functional and includes a deep stainless-steel sink, two gas burners, and a 12-volt refrigerator and freezer. The dining area is a traditional booth dinette placed under a large window, while a nearby TV mount comes in handy if your idea of entertainment involves watching some popular shows.
Photo: Forest River/ That RV Girl The bathroom is compact , as it shares the rear of the trailer with the bunk area, but it includes all the basics. It features a Thetford toilet, vanity sink, mirror, storage cabinets, and a shower with a curtain and integrated shelves for toiletries.
In terms of styling, the interior has a bright, modern residential feel with European-style flat-front cabinetry, seamless pressed countertops, woven cloth-style upholstery, and easy-to-clean vinyl flooring.
As for the numbers you need to know, this RV has a dry weight of 4,399 pounds (1,995 kg) and a GVWR rating of 6,399 pounds (2,902 kg), which leaves 2,000 pounds (907 kg) of cargo carrying capacity. It holds a fresh water tank of 39 gallons (147 liters), as well as gray and black water tanks, each with a capacity of 30 gallons (113 liters). Though it’s mainly designed for campground use, it comes pre-wired for solar expansion, supporting up to 500 watts.
No MSRP is listed on the official page of the Airlume 260 travel trailer , but actual dealer prices range between $18,499 and $27,199.

The BMW-controlled MINI brand has unleashed yet another special edition of the Countryman. Exclusive to Japan, the Nightfall Edition is a diesel-powered crossover with dark exterior detailing, a brown-and-black interior, and plenty of standard kit. Merely 200 units are in the offing, with prices kicking off at 6,000,000 yen (approximately 37,500 dollars at current exchange rates).
As with many so-called special editions from the British manufacturer, there is nothing particularly special under the skin, where you will find the Countryman D's powertrain completely unchanged. A dedicated launch event for the Nightfall Edition is due on November 14 and 15, and yes, all 200 units come in RHD.
Nightfall implies the transition from dusk into darkness, and the Slate Blue paintwork definitely evokes the deepening blue of the evening sky. A black roof and black-painted mirror caps add to the visual theme, and then there's Piano Black for the exterior trim pieces that remove most of the otherwise bright trim. 19-inch John Cooper Works Runway Spoke black wheels are on the menu as well.
Not exactly look-at-me special, but I and many other enthusiasts certainly dig the restrained approach. Truth be told, MINI doesn't need another collection of decorative stripes and oversized graphics to help the Countryman stand out in the crowd. It's already a looker, and the combination of dark blue and black perfectly suits it without turning the Nightfall Edition into a rolling accessories catalog.
The cabin receives pretty restrained updates as well, with MINI combining a predominantly black interior with Vescin Vintage Brown upholstery to create a bi-tone environment. Vescin is the MINI way of saying 100 percent vegan synthetic leather. Moving on, the Favoured trim adds John Cooper Works body-hugging seats and a sporty steering wheel to this Japanese market-only model.
Photo: MINI Electric adjustments for the front seats are standard as well, along with an active driver's seat, driver's seat memory, and rear privacy glass. The list continues with a Harman Kardon audio system, an interior camera, adaptive cruise control with stop & go, lane-departure warning, hands-off driving assistance on highways, lane-change warning, and collision-avoidance braking with steering assist.
Another piece of the active safety package includes cross-traffic warning. Parking Assistant Plus, meanwhile, handles low-speed maneuvering. PAP includes protection against unintended acceleration caused by incorrect pedal operation, 360-degree cameras, and automatic parallel plus perpendicular parking assist. According to MINI Japan, the four-pot diesel underhood is good for 150 ps at 4,000 rpm and no more than 360 Nm between 1,500 and 2,500 rpm.
Only available with two pedals, the 148-horsepower turbo diesel offers the kind of low-down torque that should make the Nightfall Edition perfect for most everyday driving scenarios. In the combined test cycle, said BMW-sourced engine tops 17.4 kilometers per liter of dinosaur juice, a figure that can be read as 5.7 liters per 100 kilometers in Europe or 40.9 miles per gallon in the US.
The Countryman is MINI 's best-selling model worldwide, and its popularity is extremely obvious in the SUV-driven market. Fuel is a big part of the story. The national average price of diesel was $6.10 a gallon on Nov. 12, up from $3.76 a year earlier, according to AAA data cited by CBS News . CBS tied the jump to higher global oil prices linked to the war in Iran .
USPS is also still losing money. The agency reported a $6.5 billion net loss for fiscal 2026, down from $9 billion the year before, Supply Chain 24/7 reported . USPS said its shipping prices are set mainly by market conditions and that the new pricing is part of its ongoing modernization plan.
January's changes cap a busy year of USPS price moves. Published Ground Advantage rates rose about 7.8% in January 2026. In July, USPS changed how it calculates dimensional weight , raising costs for some bulky, lightweight packages. Then on Oct. 18, 7,625 ZIP codes that previously received standard pricing moved into a new rate group for discounted Ground Advantage labels sold through eBay, according to Value Added Resource .
Other changes in the filing
Fees for some special services are changing, including address enhancement and premium forwarding. Competitive PO Box prices won't change in January. USPS is adding an optional Outbound Proof of Delivery service for Priority Mail International and extending Delivered Duty Paid service to International Priority Airmail. Stamp prices aren't changing.
What shippers should do
The PRC still has to review the proposal (Docket No. CP2027-1). In the meantime, shippers can use the proposed January rate tables to see what their most common shipments would cost. Sellers that offer free or flat-rate shipping can use those estimates to see whether their current thresholds still cover postage.
USPS plans to review the surcharge in July based on fuel prices in the first half of 2027, which means shipping costs could shift midyear again.

Every career has a story. In Leadership Lessons , supply chain leaders reflect on the experiences that shaped who they are and how they lead.
What’s Related
Edmund Zagorin’s first business began with a competition he thought he could win. As a college student short on cash, he learned about a business plan contest. Contestants would speak for eight minutes, then answer questions. To someone who had spent years in competitive debate, the format sounded familiar.
Zagorin called a friend with a proposition: “Hey, I think I could win some money. Do you want to start a company with me?” His friend agreed, and the two went on to build a 3D video hardware product and run a film studio in Detroit.
Today, Zagorin is Chief Strategy Officer and co-founder of Arkestro, a predictive procurement company that uses AI to help enterprises make more strategic purchasing decisions. He once expected to make a career of coaching debate teams. Years later, he was taking buses to visit customers to stretch a young company’s savings. Debate was the starting point for much of it.
Finding a place on the debate team
Zagorin was born in France to American parents who met while working as journalists. When he was five, an assignment brought the family to Washington, D.C. He remembers arriving in the United States as a young child and feeling like everyone else already belonged and that he needed to figure out where he fit.
He eventually found that place on his high school debate team. His coach sparked his interest in debate, and having friends on the team helped him stay involved despite poor early results.
“When I started debating, I was probably one of the worst debaters in the country,” he says. He kept going because he loved debating, and by the time he graduated high school, he had won a national championship.
The improvement mattered beyond the trophy. He had found something he wanted to work at, and competition gave him a way to see that work paying off.
He came to understand that the strongest competitors were “the best listeners, not the best talkers.” Listening meant being curious enough to take another person’s perspective seriously, giving their arguments credence, and responding with data , evidence, and research .
He had seen how debate could make people arrogant, but his experience took him in a different direction. “I actually thought that debate helped me find myself,” he says.
Leaving the career he thought he wanted
More Leadership Lessons
Lindsay Azim, Gartner
Steve Liou, CEO of Clarium
Jackie Wu, Corvus Robotics
Peter Bollinger, CEO of EPG
Peter Bennett, Cardinal Health
View all Leadership Lessons stories
He later became assistant director of debate at the University of Iowa. Although he enjoyed teaching, he wanted to broaden his horizons, live somewhere different and work in technology . A friend in San Francisco suggested joining a startup.
Zagorin wasn’t sure where he would fit because he wasn’t a software engineer or computer programmer. His friend suggested data science, which he had studied as an undergraduate while researching how social movements use the Internet. In 2015, he moved to San Francisco and joined a startup focused on procurement.
Finding procurement
Procurement was not entirely unfamiliar. At Iowa, Zagorin had taken the university’s procurement training.. He knew about purchasing policies and procedures, but the startup showed him how much data businesses collect and what it can reveal about how they buy.
He later worked in procurement consulting, negotiating purchases that included chemicals and road salt. “I enjoy the work of analyzing spend, figuring out a strategy, and executing it,” he says. He enjoyed the conversations with suppliers that were part of reaching a deal.
Working in procurement gave Zagorin a closer look at how companies spend their money. “Procurement and supply chain are really the largest flows of capital in the world, but they’re not often flowing with great intention,” he says. “That’s partly because the legacy systems and processes were built for compliance and control, rather than value creation and scalable speed.”
He also came to appreciate how little recognition the people making those supply chain decisions received. “I think supply chain people work really hard and don’t always get a lot of credit or appreciation, so I’ve always found common cause with that,” he says.
During the pandemic, more people began to understand his work, including his own family. “ COVID was definitely the first time my mom knew what I did for work,” he says.
“Getting a good price doesn’t matter if the product never shows up.”
People who could afford basic necessities were suddenly unsure whether they could find them. Zagorin knew that uncertainty was already familiar to people who struggled to pay for what they needed. During COVID, having the money wasn’t always enough. “It was a problem that money couldn’t solve,” he says. “Getting a good price doesn’t matter if the product never shows up.”
Building Arkestro
In 2017, Zagorin and his team began developing an AI platform for procurement negotiations, the early work behind Arkestro. The idea came from his experience with sourcing teams, where someone often had a good sense of how a negotiation would end before it began. He wondered whether a machine learning model could use similar information to predict the result.
He started by testing predictions against negotiations he was conducting as a consultant. The team also examined past negotiations, comparing the model’s predictions with the actual results. When they didn’t match, they investigated what the model had missed, such as a personal relationship between a buyer and supplier.
Consulting gave the team a way to earn money while developing the technology. Companies hired them to negotiate purchases, and they used those projects to test what they were building. “That made it a little bit easier to get started just with customers and really build with customers from day one,” he says.
The first two years brought financial uncertainty. Before outside funding, the founders put their savings into the business and cut their spending to give themselves more time. Customer visits sometimes meant sleeping on a friend’s couch. “We took greyhounds instead of flights in some cases,” he says. “We’d stay with friends instead of hotels. For several months we operated from a storage room of an art collective in San Francisco. One of the first predictive negotiations we supported was in an old convent’s chapel because that was where the wifi signal was strongest.”
Looking back, Zagorin is glad he took the chance. He calls it “type two fun,” and those trips have become stories he shares with employees who joined after the early years.
Looking ahead at AI
As Arkestro’s co-founder and Chief Strategy Officer, Zagorin remains confident in its focus on predicting negotiated prices. While much of the attention around AI goes to large language models, he believes Arkestro’s experience with procurement negotiations gives it a head start. Unlike LLMs, Arkestro’s model is focused on predicting the outcome of deals using simulations of multi-party negotiations involving one buyer and one or more suppliers.
“There's a lot of really wise and caring people involved in building these AI companies.”
“Because in a predictive negotiation on Arkestro the buyer makes the first offer to the supplier, our model is somewhat unique because we both predict and influence the deal’s outcome,” says Zagorin. “It’s not like a weather forecast . Our platform is actually creating the offers used in the deal and working through the back-and-forth with multiple suppliers simultaneously. So we predict, but we also make our own weather.”
His outlook for the AI industry is more cautious. He worries that financial pressure around upcoming public offerings could push companies to put commercial interests ahead of responsible decisions about the technology.
At the same time, he sees reasons to be optimistic about the people doing the work. “There's a lot of really wise and caring people involved in building these AI companies,” he says.
He hopes they'll help steer the industry in the right direction, but he expects the next 18 to 24 months to be a wild ride. “I would advise everyone to buckle up.”

EICMA 2026 • MTPeak Stole Some of the Spotlight at EICMA 2026 With Insane Power and Retro Looks on Three Wheels
1968 Shelby Mustang GT350 Flaunts Special-Order Paint, True One-of-One Pony
24 photos
Photo: American Mustangs/YouTube
Introduced in 1965, the GT350 was the very first Mustang to wear a Shelby badge. Originally a track-prepped vehicle , the GT350 eventually morphed into a more conventional pony car. Joined by the GT500 in 1967, the GT350 remained in production through 1969, when Ford and Shelby parted ways.
While the regular Mustang was very popular at the time, the Shelby GT350 was produced in limited numbers. Shelby put together a little over 7,000 units over five model years, with a few hundred leftover cars sold in 1970. The figure includes over 1,000 GT350H Hertz rent-a-racers.
With the exception of the first model year, when only 562 units were built, the Sheby GT350 moved over 1,000 units a year. The 1968 fastback you see here is one of 1,457 examples made, which is a lot of cars for a golden-era muscle car. It's also one of 1,053 fastbacks, as well as one of only 528 vehicles fitted with the four-speed manual transmission.
It becomes rarer when we start discussing options, but there's one feature that makes this Shelby truly special. If you're familiar with Shelby Mustang, you probably already spotted it because it's in plain sight. Yes, I'm talking about the color. This bright orange hue makes this Shelby GT350 unique.
It's not because it was an unpopular color; this pony car was commissioned with a special-order paint. It shows up on the invoice, which also lists the color code as WT5014. The color is called Mustang on the said invoice, but it's actually one of the Ford Mustang's more iconic hues. It just didn't become an option until later.
The color was added to the regular palette for the 1970 model year. It was called Grabber Orange, joining a high-impact trio that also included Grabber Blue and Grabber Green.
So what's the deal with this orange color initially called Mustard? Where did it come from? Well, its origins are unclear, but it was most likely taken from Ford's fleet car color palette, as was the case with many special-order cars at the time.
Like most high-profile Mustangs, this Shelby GT350 has a detailed Marti Report. It states that three cars were finished in this special-order hue. The other two are GT500KR models, so we're indeed looking at the only GT350 out there. While a lot of cars are one-of-one classics thanks to a combination of options, mainly decided by items like a radio or other insignificant thing, this Shelby is as genuine as they get.
In addition to being unique, this Shelby is also in stunning condition. The fastback looks showroom-new, meaning it probably received an extensive restoration a while back. Both the paint and the Deluxe interior look flawless, while the engine bay is detailed to Concours level.
Speaking of the engine bay, it houses a 302-cubic-inch (4.9-liter) small-block V8 engine. 1968 was the first year for this powerplant in the Shelby GT350, which previously featured a 289-cubic-inch (4.7-liter) V8 . But even though the unit was a tad bigger, power dropped compared to the previous years.
While the 289 V8 came with 306 horsepower on tap, the 302 V8-powered Shelby was rated at only 250 horsepower. That's because the 1968 mill had fewer racing parts than the more iconic K-code 289. The Cobra intake was pretty much the only feature that set it apart from the regular 302 Mustang mill. Shelby offered a Paxton supercharger upgrade, but those cars are very rare.
Our host doesn't say much about the history of the car and whether this GT350 is up for grabs. American Mustangs is a classic car dealer specialising in high-performance Mustangs, so we may see it on their website soon (but it's not listed now). One of the two GT500KRs finished in this color was auctioned off in 2024 for $291,500 . Similarly, this GT350 is likely worth over a quarter-million bucks. Check it out in the video below.

When Ionis Pharmaceuticals’ Tryngolza undersold, investors immediately looked to Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals’ executives for answers on how they will navigate a launch in the same market.
Rival drugmaker woes, discontinued programs and upcoming make-or-break readouts were just a few of the storylines that emerged from a busy week of biotech earnings .
Below, BioSpace recaps earnings for four biotechs in the news.
Arrowhead, Ionis face uphill battle in severe hypertriglyceridemia
Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals’ investors were keenly watching the launch of Ionis Pharmaceuticals’ Tryngolza for a read through on how Redemplo might do on the market in the same indication , severe hypertriglyceridemia (sHTG).
Ionis reported flat sales of just $9 million for the drug on Monday, and the company lowered sales guidance for the year to $50 million, with a slower ramp factored in.
Arrowhead’s investors were left dismayed. “Ultimately the Tryngolza print this week was even worse than what were already low expectations,” Stifel wrote in a note on Arrowhead’s earnings on Thursday.
Arrowhead has submitted Redemplo to the FDA in sHTG, earning entry to a new agency program that could accelerate the decision, according to the company’s fiscal year 2026 earnings report. The FDA’s Split Real Time Application Review (STAR) pilot program offers drugs that demonstrate an improvement over available therapies a shot at a faster review.
C-suite
Caught In Sarepta ‘Downdraft,’ Arrowhead Becomes RNAi Knight in Shining Armor
Sarepta’s troubles had nothing to do with Arrowhead’s assets, and yet both companies have seen their stock prices decline this past month. BioSpace caught up with Arrowhead’s Chris Anzalone to talk about the biotech’s role as an RNAi pipeline savior.
August 12, 2025
·
7 min read
·
Annalee Armstrong
Read more
The company is now preparing a second quarter launch for Redemplo in sHTG. Executives brushed off their competitors’ troubles during a Thursday earnings call.
“What we learned from Ionis doesn’t affect our expectation in sHTG at all. I think what we’ve seen from them are some missteps in communication, some missteps in commercial execution, and we don’t expect to have those missteps,” CEO Chris Anzalone said.
The chief executive expressed confidence that Redemplo will offer a differentiated profile, and early launch results for the drug in familial chylomicronemia syndrome have buoyed sentiment.
Fiscal year 2026 was the first that Arrowhead recorded full sales for Redemplo after its approval for familial chylomicronemia syndrome in November 2025 . The drug brought in $6.6 million, which executives were happy with.
Still, analysts were wary of the “tricky setup” for the impending sHTG launch. Jefferies estimates the drug could still reach $2.5 billion in sales.
“We do acknowledge the near-term setup is tricky as it’ll take time to disprove the negative here—and while there’s an appreciation that ARWR has a compelling pipeline/platform, these programs are earlier and it’s harder to point to one catalyst that’ll meaningfully change the narrative near-term,” Jefferies wrote.
Kyverna ices new manufacturing program as miv-cel reaches FDA
Kyverna Therapeutics tightened up its pipeline as the cell therapy company awaits an FDA approval for miv-cel in stiff person syndrome. The biotech has deprioritized KYV-102, which uses the same CAR backbone as miv-cel but with a different manufacturing process.
The KYV-102 program was considered a next-gen approach to miv-cel that eliminated the need for a procedure called apheresis, during which patients’ blood is removed and separated into white and red blood cells and plasma, and then the remaining components are returned to the body. The therapy also cut down on culture time, manufacturing costs and increased scalability, according to a 2025 company presentation .
An investigational new drug application was filed for the drug at the end of 2025 and accepted in early 2026 . Kyverna had planned to share the development strategy for the drug later this year.
CAR T
Weighing the risks of CAR T in autoimmune disease as Kyverna nears market
Not a month after reports of three deaths in autoimmune trials for Novartis’ CAR T cell therapy ignited a debate about the use of these treatments in nonfatal diseases, Kyverna Therapeutics reported data bolstering its case to bring to market the first CAR T for an autoimmune disease.
October 5, 2026
·
5 min read
·
Heather McKenzie
Read more
The new manufacturing process represented “a real important advance for improving patient access and will allow us to start the CAR T journey for patients even closer to their homes,” CEO Warner Biddle said in March at the Leerink Global Healthcare Conference.
This process would have aided the movement of cell therapy into more common conditions, Biddle explained at the time. “This is going to provide a lot more opportunities and flexibility for how we commercialize this and bring this to more patients,” he said.
But now the program has been iced, with Kyverna putting its eggs in the miv-cel basket.
A biologics license application for that program requesting priority review has officially been accepted for review by the FDA in stiff-person syndrome, the company announced during earnings. The review acceptance sets Kyverna up to possibly gain the first-ever cell therapy approval for an autoimmune condition.
Executives gave analysts details on the commercial launch preparations for that therapy and expansion opportunities into other indications like myasthenia gravis, rheumatoid arthritis and multiple sclerosis. “Despite recent safety concerns from third-party CAR-T programs in autoimmune diseases, we remain constructive on miv-cel given its consistent safety profile and supportive longer-term follow-up to date,” William Blair wrote on Thursday.
Prime-d for a pinnacle year with Wilson’s, AATD catalysts
Prime Medicine is poised for a possibly momentous year, with the stock rising 18% over the past six months along with interest in its Wilson’s disease drug, Jefferies wrote on Friday morning.
Dosing got underway for a Phase 1/2 clinical trial of PM577a in Wilson’s in October, the company reported during third quarter earnings on Thursday. Initial data are expected in 2027.
The next year will provide critical de-risking and proof-of-concept events for investors, Jefferies said. Prime has no gene therapy or editing competitors for Wilson’s, while the alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATD) program will face a more crowded space that includes Beam Therapeutics and CRISPR Therapeutics.
FDA
Plug-and-play gene therapy: FDA executes on vision that’s been in the works for years
Former biologics boss Peter Marks had a vision. With the FDA’s latest draft guidance, it’s coming to fruition. Speaking with BioSpace, current CBER leader Karim Mikhail said the “adapted pathway” is designed to develop personalized gene therapies more quickly.
November 2, 2026
·
6 min read
·
Heather McKenzie
Read more
Beam in particular has been a thorn in the side of Prime, with litigation regarding a contract agreement between the two resolved in July. The companies spun out of the same Harvard lab run by famed gene editing pioneer David Liu. Prime triumphed in the arbitration , with the panel ruling that the prime editing biotech has rights to PM647.
This allowed Prime to move forward with an investigational new drug (IND) application for the program in AATD, which was cleared by the FDA in September. The study will now move forward in the U.S., in which Prime estimates about 100,000 people carry the PiZZ genotype that PM647 is designed to fix.
Elsewhere, Prime will file a BLA for PM359 in chronic granulomatous disease in the first half of 2027.
“With recent financing extending cash runway through 2027, the path to value inflection points in 2027 are appealing,” Jefferies wrote.
Cullinan to unwrap autoimmune data this Christmas
T cell engager specialist Cullinan Therapeutics is facing a hectic Christmas season, with two clinical trials set to read out and a lung cancer drug already under FDA review, according to a third quarter earnings report .
Data from the Phase 1/2 trial of CLN-978 in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and Sjögren’s disease will be presented via webcast in December. The initial readout will focus on early clinical activity, biomarkers and safety, William Blair wrote in a Tuesday note.
The analyst will be looking for durability of B cell depletion with repeat dosing, more consistent remission-level responses and a clear dose response. This would inform dose selection for a later Phase 2 trial and more clinical trials in RA and SLE.
Phase 1 data for CLN-049 will be delivered at the ASH Annual Meeting on December 13.
Lung cancer
Despite 3 patient deaths, Cullinan-Taiho plan FDA filing for lung cancer pill on survival benefit
Analysts believe Cullinan Therapeutics and Taiho Oncology can overcome the safety risks as zipalertinib “sets [a] new bar” for first-line treatment of a type of lung cancer. The candidate is already under review for the the second-line setting, with a decision expected by early next year.
September 15, 2026
·
3 min read
·
Tristan Manalac
Read more
Cullinan also officially kicked off a Phase 1/2 study of velinotamig for autoimmune cytopenias in October. The therapy is also being tested in immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) and warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia.
Meanwhile, Cullinan’s partner Taiho is working on an NDA for zipalertinib in first-line EGFR ex20ins non-small cell lung cancer, while one for relapsed EGFR ex20ins NSCLC is under review with a decision date of February 27.
With so much coming up, William Blair expressed surprise at the 25% decline in Cullinan’s shares this month.
“We continue to view the recent pullback as unwarranted and [Cullinan] an attractive buying opportunity, particularly ahead of key data catalysts for CLN-978 and CLN-049 over the remainder of the year,” William Blair wrote. “We believe these, in addition to zipalertinib and velinotamig updates, have the potential to drive significant upside from current levels.”

The Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration has removed 133 electronic logging devices from its registry, citing widespread compliance failures and evidence that some systems were being used to falsify truck drivers’ hours-of-service records.
The enforcement action, announced Thursday by Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, targeted devices that federal investigators said allowed trucking companies to manipulate driving records, conceal violations of federally mandated rest periods and evade safety regulations.
Of the 133 devices removed , 121 were revoked by FMCSA, while another 12 were voluntarily withdrawn by their providers after failing to meet the administration’s readiness standards.
The crackdown comes as federal regulators intensify scrutiny of trucking safety, driver qualifications and electronic logging systems amid concerns that fraudulent records allow carriers to operate outside federal safety requirements.
As FreightWaves reported in May , FMCSA had removed 79 electronic logging devices from its registered list since January 2025, including 12 devices revoked in a single May enforcement action.
At the time, the agency’s registered ELD list contained approximately 1,050 devices, while its revoked list exceeded 250.
FMCSA did not identify the carriers involved in its most recent investigation, or disclose how many drivers used the affected systems or provided any details connecting individual devices to specific crashes.
FMCSA outlined three examples of alleged ELD fraud discovered during the investigations.
In one case, investigators said they found that an ELD provider allowed motor carriers to call a customer support line and manually erase recorded driving time, replacing it with fabricated rest periods even while drivers remained behind the wheel.
Another provider allegedly uploaded falsified driving logs during an active roadside inspection, concealing evidence that a driver had exceeded federally permitted operating hours.
A third company’s logging records showed trucks traveling at mathematically impossible speeds of up to 130 mph, which investigators said was used to compress recorded driving time, according to FMCSA.
Federal hours-of-service regulations generally limit property-carrying commercial drivers to 11 hours of driving after 10 consecutive hours off duty, with additional restrictions on driving windows and weekly operating hours.
ELDs are designed to automatically record driving time and other vehicle operating information, making it more difficult to falsify records than traditional paper logbooks.
FMCSA said motor carriers using the affected devices have up to 60 days to replace them with compliant ELDs from the agency’s registered devices list.
FMCSA said devices may be returned to the registered list if providers correct all identified deficiencies.
The agency has not disclosed how many motor carriers or commercial drivers will be affected by the removal of the 133 devices.
Why it matters: Trucking companies using the affected devices face replacement costs and potential out-of-service violations as federal regulators intensify scrutiny of electronic driver logs.

ROME — Italy has hiked its spending on the GCAP fighter this year while reducing funding for new army tanks and fighting vehicles, newly released spending documents have revealed.
Rome has spent €875 million ($970 million) in 2026 on GCAP – the program for a sixth-generation fighter which teams Italy with the United Kingdom and Japan.
That is up on last year’s €625 million and far higher than the €275 million that planners writing in last year’s budget document predicted would be spent in 2026.
The new numbers are contained in the much delayed Italian defense budget for 2026, which was sent by the defense ministry to parliament this week for approval.
Defense News has seen the part of the document containing the breakdown on costs per program, but not the section listing total spending.
The GCAP nations in July handed a £4.6 billion ($6.1 billion) development contract to their national champions building the jet after the U.K. freed up delayed cash.
The 18-month contract went to Edgewing, the industrial consortium grouping the firms building the fighter. Germany is reportedly now mulling signing up after the collapse of its plan to build the FCAS jet with France.
The 2026 budget document, which contains spending forecasts, predicts Italy will spend €696 million on the GCAP program in 2027.
Meanwhile spending on heavy army vehicles in 2026 was lower than forecast, despite Italy working on a new main battle tank and fighting vehicle with Rheinmetall.
The program envisages the delivery of 1,050 Lynx vehicles and 272 Panther tanks as part of a €23 billion euro deal. But in July, Italian defense minister Guido Crosetto said Italy would cut 18% in costs from the program.
The new document puts spending on the two new programs, as well as upgrades to Italy’s ageing Ariete tanks, at €177 million in 2026, lower than last year’s €281 million and far lower than the €425 million that last year’s document predicted would be spent in 2026.
By way of compensation, this year’s budget predicts a major hike in spending on the three programs to €872 million in 2027.
Although Defense News has not seen the section of the budget giving total expenditures, a tally of the costs of the individual program outlays this year amounts to €12.8 billion, up by €307 million from the €12.5 billion given by totaling all the programs in the 2025 budget.
Italy’s F-35 program, which involves the eventual purchase of 115 aircraft, cost Italy €782 million in 2026, less than the the €961 million planners last year forecast it would receive.
This year’s budget document has been the focus of heated political debate as defense spending comes under the spotlight ahead of Italian national elections next year, which will see incumbent right wing prime minister Giorgia Meloni seeking reelection.
Meloni’s arguments in favor of defense spending have come under fire from both her allies and foes, including Matteo Salvini, the head of League party which forms part of Meloni’s coalition, and Robert Vannacci, a former army general running a new party to the right of Meloni.
Among opposition parties, the Five Star party has also criticized defense spending, claiming they are diverting scarce funds from health spending.
Students who have recently taken to the streets in Italy as part of a Europe-wide wave of street protests have listed a cut to arms spending as one of their main aims.
The opposition to arms spending has coincided with growing opposition to supplying arms to Ukraine, a policy Meloni has fought for since her election in 2022.

Regeneron’s mid-stage success in postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome has the company gearing up to launch a Phase 3 study in the first half of 2027.
A single dose of Regeneron Pharmaceuticals’ investigational monoclonal antibody reduced orthostatic heart rate at eight days for patients with a common autonomic nervous system disorder that causes abnormal heart rate elevations when standing.
Regeneron’s Phase 2 Pinnacle trial enrolled 82 patients with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS), a chronic condition that is also associated with lightheadedness, brain fog and fatigue. There are currently no FDA-approved treatments available to treat the disorder.
Pinnacle met its primary goal measuring the change in heart rate from lying down to standing at day eight, according to data presented Thursday at the American Autonomic Society annual meeting in San Diego.
Patients receiving a single 450-mg injection of baloncibart—also known as REGN7544—experienced a mean drop in heart rate of 11.4 beats per minute compared to placebo, while a 150-mg injection reduced heart rate by 9.5 beats per minute.
Patients receiving the high dose continued to experience a significant decrease in heartbeat at day 29, while those on the lower dose did not.
Regeneron also recorded improvements for the 450-mg arm on measures like physical functioning and daily living activities at day 29, as reported by patients. No improvements were observed for the 150-mg cohort on these measures compared to placebo.
The experimental 450-mg dose was generally well tolerated, with treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) mostly mild or moderate. One severe TEAE occurred in the placebo arm, while one serious TEAE of headache occurred in the 150-mg cohort and one case of fainting was reported for the 450-mg dose. None of the TEAEs prompted discontinuation from the study.
Regeneron now plans on moving baloncibart into late-stage testing, with a trial launch slated for the first half of next year.
“POTS is a condition that disproportionately impacts younger women and has been under-recognized and under-served for too long, which is why it was critical to incorporate the patient experience in our trial design and measure symptoms that reflect how patients actually feel and function,” Boaz Hirshberg, senior vice president of clinical development and internal medicine at Regeneron, said in a release.
The cause of POTS remains unclear, though it is believed to be tied to low blood volume, according to Regeneron. Baloncibart is an NPR1-blocking monoclonal antibody designed to increase the volume of blood in circulation to reduce the increased heart rate and subsequent symptoms.
Both doses of baloncibart at day eight were associated with “biomarkers consistent with the anticipated beneficial plasma volume expansion driven by NPR1 blockade,” according to the company.
