Volkswagen is getting ready to bring a €20,000 ($22,000) electric car to market in 2027, and it looks like the entry-level EV may no longer be nameless. A newly filed trademark could have just given away what VW plans to call it.
Volkswagen trademarks ID. UP as potential entry-level EV
The new entry-level EV is “the last piece of the puzzle,” Volkswagen brand CEO Thomas Schäfer said last March after unveiling the ID. EVERY1 concept car.
Volkswagen said the production version will launch in 2027 with a starting price of around €20,000 ($22,000).
The new model will sit below the ID. Polo in Volkswagen’s Electric Urban Car Family, a lineup of compact, affordable electric cars.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Volkswagen’s current entry-level EV lineup includes the ID. Polo, ID. Cross, the Cupra Raval, and Skoda Epiq, all based on its new MEB+ platform.
After launching the lower-priced standard versions of the ID. Polo and ID. Cross recently, starting at €24,995 and €27,995, respectively, Volkswagen is preparing to launch an even smaller, more affordable EV next year.
A recent trademark filing with the European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO) and the German DPMA may have just revealed the name of VW’s upcoming €20,000 EV.
Volkswagen trademark application for the name ID. UP (Source: EUIPO)
Volkswagen filed a trademark application for the name ID. UP on October 22, 2026, with the EUIPO and DPMA, suggesting this will be the name of the upcoming electric car in 2027.
The trademark follows previous reports that VW planned to revive the former Up! name as part of its shift away from its previous numerical naming scheme (ID.3, ID.4, ID.5, etc.).
Volkswagen has kept most details a secret thus far. Like the ID. Polo, the first to go on sale with an established VW nameplate, the ID. UP is expected to use the same 37 kWh LFP battery to reduce costs.
VW Brand CEO Thomas Schäfer introduces the ID. EVERY1 concept car (Source: Volkswagen)
The VW ID. Polo with the 37 kWh battery offers a WLTP range of up to 334 km (207 miles), so the smaller ID. UP will likely provide around the same, if not slightly more.
Volkswagen said it will offer at least 250 km (155 miles) of range. It will also use a new 70 kW (94 hp) electric motor, enabling a top speed of 130 km/h (80 mph).
The production version of the ID. EVERY1, expected to arrive as the ID. UP, will be one of nine new models VW plans to launch by 2027.
Volkswagen ID. EVERY1 concept car (Source: Volkswagen)
Volkswagen previously said the entry-level EV will be 3,880 mm long, which would position it between the former Up! (3,600 mm) and the ID. Polo (4,053 mm). Despite its compact size, VW said the electric city car will seat four passengers and offer a luggage compartment volume of 305 liters.
The VW Group’s new Electric Urban Car Family is off to a strong start, securing nearly 150,000 orders after series production began in June.
All models within the family are built on the MEB+ platform with a FWD powertrain, and share more than 80% of the components and tech.
Volkswagen ID. EVERY1 concept car interior (Source: Volkswagen)
Volkswagen said the production version of the ID. EVERY1 will be among the first vehicles based on its zonal software-defined vehicle (SDV) architecture, which is being developed through its joint venture with Rivian.
In March, the Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies (RV Tech) joint venture tested the new SDV architecture on the ID. EVERY1, alongside Audi and Scout reference vehicles, validating over-the-air (OTA) capabilities.
The new architecture will enable “highly automated driving features” and “advanced infotainment solutions,” with continuous OTA updates.
While VW said it will deploy the SDV architecture in “electric vehicles across markets in the Western Hemisphere,” the entry-level EV is not expected to reach the States.
Volkswagen is, however, preparing to launch the ID. Tiguan , which will launch in 2027 as the successor to the ID.4 (and ID.5 in Europe).

By: Northern Miner Staff November 13, 2026
Aris Mining (TSX, NYSE: ARIS) raised the estimated construction cost of its Toroparu gold project in Guyana by 36% to $1.1 billion (C$1.6 billion), while extending its operating plan and maintaining an early 2027 target for a construction decision.
The prefeasibility study, released after markets closed Thursday , outlines 5.6 million oz. of gold production over 29 years of processing, including 258,000 oz. annually in the first 17 years. BMO and National Bank mining analysts said the larger project helps offset the higher capital bill. The earlier plan outlined 5 million oz. over 21 years. The revised schedule includes 21 years of mining.
“We currently estimate that the company will be able to internally finance the remaining capital required through its existing cash flow,” BMO mining analyst Brian Quast said Friday in a note.
Toroparu would add a major producing asset in Guyana to a company expanding its Colombian mines towards combined annual output of 500,000 oz. The next hurdle is permitting: Aris needs a large-scale mining licence and other approvals before committing to a 32-month build.
Detailed engineering
Construction capital, including contingency, has risen by $299 million from the $820 million estimated in the 2025 preliminary economic assessment. The new plan replaces an owner-operated leased mining fleet with contractors.
More detailed engineering, a longer construction schedule in a remote location, expanded infrastructure and industry inflation contributed to the increase, National Bank mining analyst Don DeMarco said in a note Thursday. Greater production early in the operating life and lower sustaining capital support the revised economics, he said.
The result is “a more conservative, execution-ready baseline fully offset by front-loaded production and stronger project economics,” DeMarco wrote.
DeMarco maintained an outperform rating and C$39 share-price target. Quast kept his outperform rating and C$48 target while lifting BMO’s valuation of Toroparu to about $2.1 billion from $1.9 billion.
Funding and returns
The company’s initial funding requirement is $1 billion. That includes $1 billion of construction capital, $102 million of contingency and $24 million of working capital, less $138 million assumed to be available under an existing precious-metals streaming agreement with Wheaton Precious Metals (TSX, NYSE, LSE: WPM). The streaming funds remain subject to Wheaton electing to proceed. The companies are exploring amendments to the agreement.
BMO expects cash generation from existing operations to cover the balance. DeMarco also pointed to liquidity, unused borrowing capacity and cash flow expected from the Marmato expansion. Aris continues to target first gold from Marmato’s new carbon-in-pulp plant in December.
At a gold price of $3,600 per oz., Toroparu has an after-tax net present value of $2.8 billion at a 5% discount rate, a 32% internal rate of return and a 2.2-year payback from the start of operations. At the same gold price, the earlier assessment’s valuation was about $2.7 billion, DeMarco said.
The earlier study’s published base case used $3,000 gold, so its headline $1.8-billion valuation is not directly comparable. At $3,000 gold, the new study also values Toroparu at about $1.8 billion.
Toroparu’s average production is expected to reach 291,000 oz. annually over the first five years. Output is projected to average 195,000 oz. over the full processing life as lower-grade stockpiles enter the plant later in the schedule. Life-of-project all-in sustaining costs are pegged at $1,494 per oz., up from $1,289 previously, while estimated sustaining capital fell 57% to $459 million, DeMarco said.
Larger resource
The study also establishes Aris’s first reserve estimate for the project. Toroparu is estimated to hold 200.2 million proven and probable tonnes grading 0.92 gram gold per tonne for 5.92 million oz. of contained gold.
The resource contains 360.9 million measured and indicated tonnes at 0.80 gram gold per tonne for 9.25 million oz., inclusive of reserves. Another 115.4 million inferred tonnes at 0.68 gram gold contain 2.54 million oz.
The 74% increase in measured and indicated gold reflects a higher resource gold price, lower cut-off grades and the inclusion of lower-grade material, DeMarco said. The resource uses $2,600 gold, compared with $1,950 previously. The new reserve estimate uses $1,950 gold.
Toroparu lies about 215 km southwest of Georgetown, in Guyana’s Cuyuni-Mazaruni region, according to Aris’s annual information form. The company applied for its large-scale mining licence in August.
Aris shares rose 0.1% to C$21.11 Friday morning in Toronto, valuing the company at about C$4.4 billion. The stock has traded between C$14.98 and C$31.47 over the past year.

Triple-Black C-Body: 1968 Chrysler New Yorker Is Amazingly Original, 440 V8 Included

Photo: Steve Magnante/YouTube
When it comes to Mopars from the 1960s, we often think about the B-body muscle cars . And that's mainly because these vehicles are more desirable due to their high-performance powerplants and, in many cases, rarity. But the C-body full-size cars were just as remarkable at the time.
Chrysler debuted the C-body architecture for the 1965 model year. It utilized a torsion bar front suspension design, which made the cars much more stable than their predecessors. The Mopars also delivered a very smooth ride and were often compared favorably to the competition.
The C-body's arrival also coincided with the slab-sided look designed by Elwood Engel. All full-sized Mopars employed a more modern appearance with lower, wider profiles, as well as a notably larger glass area. In 1969, the C-body cars pioneered the "fuselage" design language that found its way on B-body Mopars in 1971.
The platform came with seven different wheelbase sizes, ranging from 119 to 127 inches. The shorter platform was used by Plymouth, whereas the longest iteration was reserved for range-topping Imperial models . The C-body platform remained in use until 1978 (the B-body architecture was phased out a year later).
The Chrysler division used three sizes. The station wagons built in 1965-1966 employed a 121-inch version, while the 1967-1973 Town & Country rode on the 122-inch platform. Everything else was built on the 124-inch layout (including the 300, Newport, and New Yorker).
The New Yorker, one of Chrysler's most iconic and longest-running nameplates, was produced for three generations on the C-body platform. The two-door coupe you see here rolled off the assembly line in 1968, right before the New Yorker adopted the "fuselage" styling.
Although I'm a big fan of the latter, the 1968 New Yorker has its own thing going thanks to a few updates introduced that year, including the revised front sheet metal and bumpers. But more importantly, this New Yorker is one of those unrestored survivors we don't see very often.
The Mopar was discovered by classic car enthusiast Steve Magnante at an automotive shop in Hubbardston, Massachusetts. It has been sitting for about ten years, but it hasn't been neglected. And even though it's nearly 60 years old as of 2026, it's still in very good shape. This includes the original paint, the vinyl top, and the interior. Oh, it's also a legit triple-black classic.
The good news extends under the hood, which contains the numbers-matching 440-cubic-inch (7.2-liter) V8. The RB was the only unit available in 1968, with two flavors available. The standard K-code unit came with 350 horsepower on tap, while the optional L-code "TNT" variant delivered 375 horsepower. This New Yorker packs the former.
The vehicle is apparently for sale, but there's no address or website to check it out in detail. However, our host provides a phone number you can call toward the end of the video. Hit the play button to check out what has to be one of the finest 1968 New Yorker survivors out there.

By: Noah Chaikin November 13, 2026
A longer trade truce with China could ease manufacturers’ rare earth supply fears while making potential Canadian alternatives harder to finance. On Nov. 9, Beijing extended the suspension of its broader October 2025 restrictions on rare earth exports worldwide until Jan. 10, 2027, matching its trade truce with Washington. Licensing rules introduced in April 2025 remain in force, including those affecting permanent magnets used in electric motors.
Access to established Chinese suppliers gives manufacturers a reason to postpone supply agreements with Canadian mine developers that could require testing new materials and accepting higher prices. Neither Wicheeda nor Strange Lake is producing. Buyers would be committing to future supply, helping developers obtain the financing needed to build their projects.
Government financing commitments for critical minerals reached about $65 billion (C$91.8 billion) in advanced economies in 2025, more than four times their 2023 level, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA). Capital spending fell 9% that year among 24 major mining companies tracked by the agency, with battery metals driving the decline. For Canadian rare earth developers, public backing still needs to be matched by customers willing to commit to alternative supply.
Easing Chinese controls could leave committed buyers paying more than competitors who hold off, the University of Sydney’s United States Studies Centre warned in September . The centre linked difficulty securing buyers to years of delay before Arafura Rare Earths’ (ASX: ARU) May 2026 investment decision for its Nolans project in Australia. Arafura requires binding sales agreements covering 80% of planned neodymium and praseodymium production before drawing senior debt, demonstrating why buyer hesitation can hold up financing.
Projects need offtakes
Defense Metals’ (TSXV: DEFN; US-OTC: DFMTF) proposed Wicheeda rare earth project in British Columbia received Export Development Canada’s June 2025 expression of interest in arranging up to $250 million in development and construction loans. Financing remains conditional on the lender’s project review, while a May 2026 supply and investment memorandum with South Korea’s Hanwha Ocean (KRX: 042660) and Hanwha Corp. (KRX: 000880) doesn’t guarantee purchases.
Those discussions need to produce binding sales of mixed rare earth carbonate for further separation, supporting Wicheeda’s target of completing a feasibility study and securing offtake in 2027 before closing financing in 2028.
Torngat Metals signed a 10-year agreement with French processor Carester in October 2025 for its Strange Lake project in northern Quebec, demonstrating that some buyers are already making long-term commitments to diversify. The contract covers a partially separated stream containing dysprosium and terbium for Carester’s Caremag subsidiary.
Torngat is seeking additional buyers for separated oxides from its proposed operation. Up to C$165 million of public lending announced in June 2025 supports preconstruction work, leaving the larger construction financing package to be assembled. Torngat is targeting mine commissioning in 2030, subject to regulatory approvals.
These examples show why customer commitments matter to financing; they do not establish that trade truces have delayed either Canadian project. The risk is that further extensions encourage buyers to postpone contracts or seek shorter terms, weakening the sales commitments available to support construction loans.
Supporting future supply
To sustain investment through further truces, Ottawa should negotiate pooled purchases with allied processors and magnet manufacturers, using capped public support to secure contracts with Canadian suppliers. Combining orders would spread the commitment across creditworthy companies, each responsible for specified quantities at minimum prices over a period that supports debt repayment. Processors would provide the link between Canadian mine output and the oxides magnet manufacturers require. Automakers should help fund those commitments, since tripling rare earth prices would add just 0.1% to a car’s price, according to the IEA.
Japan has already linked public backing with industrial purchases through Japan Australia Rare Earths, a joint venture of its state metals agency and trading house Sojitz (TSE: 2768). Its March 2026 agreement commits to buying 5,000 tonnes of neodymium and praseodymium annually from Lynas Rare Earths (ASX: LYC) through 2038 at a $110-per-kg floor. The arrangement gives Lynas predictable sales volumes and a minimum price.
Ottawa should assess whether the Canada Critical Minerals Accelerator could help finance similar purchasing agreements for Canadian rare earths, with allied governments sharing the cost. Its C$2 billion is an announced five-year allocation, with investments approved individually. Competitive bids would set a fixed public payment per unit to Canadian suppliers, payable against verified deliveries within agreed volume and time limits.
For illustration, a contract for a specified rare earth oxide might guarantee the supplier $100 per kg, with governments contributing $20 and the buyer paying $80. If equivalent Chinese material fell to $60 per kg, those obligations would remain unchanged. Public payments would be made only against verified deliveries within the agreed support limits.
Buyers would bear the risk of cheaper competing supply, while developers would remain responsible for construction and delivery.
For deliveries outside the public support limits, buyers would pay the full agreed minimum price, with no further taxpayer contribution.
Price support could lift the internal rate of return of a typical rare earth refinery outside China by about 2.4 percentage points at an average annual public cost of $18 million, according to IEA modelling .
Canada’s mineral future cannot depend on another disruption in Chinese supply. Beijing may extend its suspension again beyond Jan. 10, so Ottawa should use the Nov. 18–19 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders’ meeting in Shenzhen, China, to begin negotiations with allies on pooled purchase contracts. Those contracts would help Canadian projects secure construction financing even if relations with China improve.
Noah Chaikin is a strategy consultant in Kearney’s Foresight practice in Toronto, advising executives on geopolitics, critical minerals and economic security. The author has no client relationships with the companies named in this article. The views expressed are his own.

The Trump administration is weighing another controversial extension of a temporary Jones Act waiver ahead of its Sunday expiration, potentially preserving a shipping option intended to ease fuel transportation constraints and help contain costs.
Sources who spoke on the condition of anonymity tell FreightWaves and Reuters that the administration is expected to extend the waiver. The current authorization is scheduled to expire at 11:59 p.m. ET on November 15.
The Jones Act generally requires goods moving between U.S. ports to travel aboard U.S.-built, U.S.-owned and U.S.-crewed vessels. The temporary waiver allows foreign-flagged ships to carry certain covered commodities such as fuel and fertilizer on domestic routes, rather than suspending the law across all coastwise shipping.
First introduced March 17 and subsequently extended twice following the Iran war, the waiver has operated under a case-by-case approval process since mid-August. Shippers must submit vessel, cargo and voyage information; the Maritime Administration assesses whether a qualified domestic vessel is available; and the Department of War determines whether to authorize the voyage.
According to Reuters’ sources, another extension would retain those individual-voyage reviews. The reporting did not establish how long the next extension would last.
Domestic maritime interests have urged the administration to allow the waiver to expire. The American Maritime Partnership argues that continued exemptions threaten investment in U.S. shipyards, while other industry representatives have called for waivers to be restricted to genuine national-defense needs and situations in which American vessels are unavailable.
At the same time, foreign shipowners’ interest in waiver voyages has weakened. Argus reported November 12 that tighter reviews, clarification that U.S. taxes still apply, and strong international tanker earnings have made the domestic voyages less attractive.
Some analysts have said that the waiver’s effect has been in pennies per gallon for retail gasoline prices.
The price per barrel of mainland propane shipped to Puerto Rico in July, compared with the Mont Belvieu benchmark , the primary North American wholesale pricing hub and global reference price for natural gas, was $59.14 versus $29.53, a gap of about 100% before freight costs. Before the waiver, Puerto Rico paid about $34 per barrel, according to the Transportation Institute, a pro-domestic shipping think tank, citing Puerto Rico Planning Board and U.S. Energy Information Administration data.
“[M]ost of these voyages went at premiums to current Jones Act timecharter rates because they were almost all arbitrage situations driven by the temporary dislocations,” analyst John McCown told FreightWaves.
Why it matters: The decision will determine whether shippers retain access to foreign vessels for qualifying domestic cargo movements, balancing transportation flexibility against domestic maritime investment concerns.

The Zonveer ZX3 is one of the best values I’ve seen in electric off-road riding, and one of the most fun things I’ve ridden to date – value for the dollar. Its Black Friday sale brings the 2,800W electric dirt bike down to $1,299, $500 off its $1,799 list price.
For that money, you get a 1,200Wh battery, dual hydraulic disc brakes, and full suspension in a 130 lb package. That’s a great entry point for beginners.
Zonveer ZX3 specs and price
Zonveer is a young brand. It launched in the US in March with two bikes, the kid-sized DX1 and the ZX3, and it’s run by United Mobility, which lists its address in Dover, Delaware. It sells direct and ships from US warehouses, and Zonveer also sells the ZX3 across Europe under its own brand through its EU store .
Screenshot
Here’s what the ZX3 brings, according to Zonveer’s product page :
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Motor: 2,800W peak rear hub motor (2,000W rated), 110 Nm of torque
Top speed: 37 mph, with 20 mph and 28 mph modes
Battery: 48V 25Ah (1,200Wh), removable
Claimed range: 40 to 45 miles on throttle, up to 65 miles with pedal assist
Weight: 130 lb (59 kg), with a 265 lb max load
Brakes: dual hydraulic disc brakes front and rear, 220 mm rotors
Wheels and suspension: 19-inch off-road tires, dual hydraulic suspension front and rear
Charging: about 6 hours on the included 4A charger
Price: $1,799 list, now $1,299 on sale
A hub motor means there’s no motor chain to maintain, and the NFC card and PIN unlock mean there’s no app to fight with. I like that.
Fun first, and built for lighter riders
Zonveer sent me a ZX3 to test, and I’m impressed with what they shipped, knowing the cost. It isn’t trying to be a race bike. And it doesn’t need to be. Here’s my first ride review:
With 2,800W peak, it’s somewhat modest by e-moto standards. That’s exactly what makes it approachable for someone who has never ridden a dirt bike: the power is enough to have a blast on trails without being intimidating.
My girlfriend had never ridden a dirt bike before, and she got comfortable within a few minutes, and she was hooked as soon as she got the hang of it.
And while testing with my girlfriend, it was clear this bike makes the most sense for lighter riders. Zonveer claims it climbs slopes of up to 30 degrees, which is optimistic for anyone over ~175 lbs, like myself. It still climbed some of the worst slopes on my land, but it did so with some difficulty, which wasn’t the case for some of my lighter friends who also rode it.
Range is the other claim to take with a grain of salt. Riding 45 miles on 1,200Wh means using under 27Wh per mile, which is e-bike efficiency on a 130 lb dirt bike with knobby tires. It’s still a lot of energy, and you can ride this long distances at lower speeds. Just expect less if you ride it hard, and that’s where the fun is at.
Black Friday deal
Zonveer’s Black Friday sale has the ZX3 at $1,299, and the company gave Electrek readers the code ELECTREK for an extra 5% off, which brings it down to $1,234.05.
The sale also includes a free water bottle and lock, and can be combined for a two-pack of ZX3s for $2,599. Shipping is free, the warranty is one year, Zonveer told us it accepts returns within 30 days on bikes ridden less than 10 miles, with a $200 restocking fee. Here’s the full refund policy .
Electrek’s Take
We’ve ridden a lot of electric two-wheelers, and the ZX3 is one of the most fun per dollar. At $1,299, or about $1,234 with our code, it’s hard to find another 1,200Wh electric dirt bike with dual hydraulic disc brakes and full suspension from a brand that ships from US warehouses.
It’s not fast by e-moto standards, and the range and climbing claims are optimistic. But for beginners, and especially lighter riders, the power lands right in that sweet spot of manageable fun. It’s a bike you can learn on without scaring yourself, and it’s cheap enough that a family can buy two for less than one Sur-Ron.

Proficient Auto Logistics, North America’s largest finished vehicle logistics platform, sees better days ahead, but its 2026 third quarter signaled a still-difficult operating environment for car haulers. The Jacksonville, Florida-based company pointed to several levers—higher pricing, improved fuel surcharge recovery and better-than-expected acquisition synergies—to repair margins.
Proficient ( NASDAQ: PAL ) reported a headline net loss of $10 million for the period. Excluding acquisition-related and other nonrecurring items, it recorded a modest operating profit. A 99.8% adjusted operating ratio (inverse of operating margin ) was 350 basis points worse year over year.
Shares of PAL were down 20% in early Friday trading. The stock has fallen more than 70% this year.
Table: Proficient’s key performance indicators
Revenue increased 30% y/y to $149 million. The quarter benefitted from the August acquisition of California-based Hansen & Adkins . The roughly six-week revenue contribution added $51 million to the quarter. However, third-quarter revenue from Proficient’s legacy network was down 16% y/y.
(The acquisition followed recent M&A in the space and the 2025 shutdown of Jack Cooper.)
Total vehicle deliveries increased 39% y/y with revenue per delivery (ex-fuel) down 10% y/y. The revenue mix was slightly less favorable and the addition of Hansen & Adkins lowered Proficient’s overall length of haul.
Most of the company’s contracts renew every three years and it is targeting “at least” mid-single-digit rate increases. It said rate increases averaged a little over 10% on the $25 million in contracts renewed since Sept. 1.
It’s attempting to renegotiate below-market contracts ahead of expiration, but warned it could potentially lose this business. It is also increasing spot exposure as only 7% to 12% of the volume currently moving through the network is priced above contract rates.
“Fuel surcharge under-recovery” produced near-breakeven results on the operating line.
Proficient’s OEM customers set the fuel surcharge tables, which are slow to adjust. (Diesel prices increased in nine out of 13 weeks in the third quarter, finishing the period 48% higher y/y.) Proficient said the fuel headwinds negatively impacted the OR by 200 to 250 bps.
The company also called out driver wages, recruiting and retention costs as detractors. Further, insurance and claims expenses were up 140 bps y/y as a percentage of revenue.
Proficient forecast fourth-quarter revenue of $180 million to $195 million, which was below the consensus estimate of $203 million at the time of the print. It expects to record 50 to 100 bps of sequential margin improvement in the period, roughly implying a 99% OR.
It said car inventories available for shipment near the ports are up 15%, and that it has added more than 200 new third-party carriers in the past 30 days. The Hansen & Adkins capacity integration has led to better asset utilization and more than 900 incremental units hauled per day (over $500,000 in monthly revenue).
It forecast a full-year 2027 OR of 95% to 97%, with further improvement occurring in 2028 (92% to 94%). Better pricing and fuel surcharge recovery, along with synergies from the acquisition, are the catalysts. Acquisition synergies are now expected to total $20 million to $30 million, well above the initial guide of $6 million to $10 million.
Longer term, it sees a path to a sub-90% OR.
Proficient will use cash to fund equipment replacement capex ($20 million in 2027), to pay down debt (net debt of $201 million) and to buy back stock ($13.9 million remaining on an open authorization in relation to its $73 million market cap).
Net debt leverage was approximately 4x at the end of the quarter, but is forecast to be below 3x by the end of the 2027 third quarter, as full-year EBITDA is expected to double to $60 million to $70 million.
Why it matters? There is only one publicly traded auto hauler. Proficient’s quarterly results provide a rare look at the transportation side of the automotive industry. Recent acquisitions highlight a major consolidation across the space, reshaping capacity and competitive dynamics.

ISTANBUL — Turkey and Egypt are taking steps to strengthen their cooperation in the maritime domain, with joint shipbuilding opportunities on the table.
Adm. Ercüment Tatlıoğlu, the commander of Turkey’s navy, made an announcement to that effect during the Sea of Friendship 2026 naval exercise in Alexandria, Egypt.
The exercise was conducted under the command of Egypt’s Northern Fleet from Nov. 4 to Nov. 9. The previous iteration took place in 2025, following a 13-year hiatus.
The largest warship in the Turkish Navy’s inventory, the amphibious assault ship TCG Anadolu, was among the Turkish units participating in the exercise. The drill covered surface warfare, anti-submarine warfare, air defense operations and underwater assault training.
Tatlıoğlu held talks with his Egyptian counterpart, Vice Adm. Mahmoud Adel Fawzy, on the sidelines of the event at Alexandria Naval Base on Nov. 7.
Tatlıoğlu described the Sea of Friendship exercise as a substantial demonstration of growing cooperation between Turkey and Egypt in the Eastern Mediterranean. He said the two navies were taking concrete steps to expand cooperation in unmanned aerial and naval systems, highlighting the participation of the Bayraktar TB3 unmanned aerial vehicle and the MKE Pirana one-way unmanned surface vehicle.
“We aim to take our defense industry cooperation in the maritime domain to a more advanced level by undertaking joint shipbuilding activities with Egypt, similar to the cooperation we have established with Pakistan under the MILGEM Project,” Tatlıoğlu said.
The MILGEM Project was initiated by the Turkish Navy to design and build indigenously developed naval platforms. The project has resulted in the development of Ada-class corvettes and Istanbul-class frigates, which are in service with the Turkish Navy, as well as Ada-class variants for the Pakistani, Ukrainian and Malaysian navies and a Hisar-class offshore patrol vessel for the Romanian Navy.
Meanwhile, Fawzy described this month’s exercise as well planned and executed despite sea conditions that were not particularly favorable.
“This activity demonstrates that we are on the right track,” he said. “We can train together, plan together and conduct ship-boarding activities together. We can work together. In the near future, the Egyptian and Turkish navies may be able to operate side by side, shoulder to shoulder, on joint missions.”
The naval exercise took place just 15 days after the House of Representatives in eastern Libya, based in Benghazi, unanimously ratified a Turkey–Libya maritime jurisdiction agreement on Oct 20.
The original 2019 Turkey-Libya maritime delimitation agreement is strategically important as it establishes a boundary between the two countries’ claimed continental shelves and exclusive economic zones (EEZs) in the Eastern Mediterranean.
For Turkey, this agreement is to protect its maritime jurisdiction claims and prevent Greek islands from effectively limiting Turkey’s access to maritime areas. For Libya, it provides a basis for asserting its own maritime rights.
Greece opposes the agreement, arguing that it disregards the maritime entitlements of Greek islands and undermines its claims in the Eastern Mediterranean.
In 2019, the agreement was signed only by Libya’s Government of National Accord in Tripoli. Now it has been ratified by the House of Representatives in Benghazi, thus bringing the two major parties in Libya to accept the agreement.
Even so, Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty described the pact as “completely null and void” during an Oct. 23 visit to Istanbul, where he met his Turkish counterpart, Hakan Fidan.
Serhat Güvenç, a professor of international relations at Kadir Has University in Istanbul, stated that Egypt was still unwilling to sign an agreement on exclusive economic zones (EEZs) with Turkey but was, at the same time, cooperating with Turkey in a major naval exercise in which TCG Anadolu was also participating.

Windward Bio’s public debut brings this year’s IPO count well above the sluggish total of eight in 2025.
Windward Bio is circling up $175 million in initial public offering funds, money that will push its lead program forward in asthma and another chronic lung disease.
The antibody-focused biotech’s expected gross proceeds account for nearly 10.3 million shares sold at $17 per share, according to a Thursday night release . The Swiss startup—which debuted on the Nasdaq Friday—is also giving underwriters a 30-day option to buy up to 1.5 million more shares at the IPO price.
At the same time, the biotech has generated $50 million from a private placement by Sanofi Foreign Participations B.V., a subsidiary of global pharma Sanofi. The Parisian pharma’s venture arm also participated in Windward’s $165 million series B crossover round in May.
Including the private placement, Windward will collect $225 million.
The biotech estimated that it will need up to $227.5 million to complete three trials for monoclonal anti-TSLP antibody WIN378, including potential regulatory and manufacturing activities. The asset is currently being studied in a Phase 2/3 trial for asthma and a Phase 2 trial in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), with plans for a confirmatory asthma trial expected to start in the first half of 2027. The study will evaluate WIN378’s potential as a twice-yearly treatment.
Windward’s IPO is the latest in this year’s flurry of biotech debuts, bringing the total to 35 for 2026 thus far, according to BioSpace ’s count. This includes Parabilis Medicines’ $670 million summer IPO —the largest public debut in biotech history.
So far, proceeds and exits have both surpassed yearly IPO totals from 2022 through 2025. In 2025, only eight biotechs went public for the whole year, according to BioSpace’s historical data.

Ibogaine, which operates via a “matrix pharmacology,” has long been a focus of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and the Trump administration.
The Department of Health and Human Services is full steam ahead on ibogaine. On Thursday, the department announced a range of investments in the psychedelic compound, along with other rapid-acting psychotropic drugs for serious mental illnesses, including post-traumatic stress disorder.
Up to $4.9 million will be invested through the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H) to advance these investigational medicines for PTSD “and other serious mental illnesses, including in veterans,” HHS revealed on Thursday during a Veteran’s Day announcement.
This initial commitment, which will be distributed over five years, will be followed by additional awards that will focus on ibogaine as a potential treatment for substance use disorders, according to the HHS press release. The awards, which will “vary in funding amount” per awardee, will go toward the regulatory and manufacturing groundwork for future trials.
“Veterans kept their promise to this country. We must keep ours,” Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said in a prepared statement. “Veterans have told us ibogaine changed their lives. Their experiences demand serious scientific investigation. We will pursue the evidence, confront the risks and put affordability at the center of this work.”
Additionally, the National Institute of Mental Health is offering a $20 million funding opportunity to launch a research network to study rapid-acting psychotropic interventional drugs, including ketamine, esketamine, psilocybin and other emerging treatments for serious mental illnesses. Johnson & Johnson markets an esketamine nasal spray called Spravato, which was first approved in 2019 and is now cleared for three types of severe depression.
Psychedelics
Despite FDA trial clearance, ibogaine metabolite won’t receive red carpet treatment

“Reports of successful ibogaine treatments are too promising to ignore. We owe it to our heroes and every person struggling to ask the bold questions and deliver results in years, not decades,” Al Bugazia, senior adviser for Special Projects at ARPA-H said in a prepared statement. “As long as people continue to struggle, doing anything less is not an option.”
Ibogaine has been a key focus for the Trump administration. In April, the president issued an executive order to accelerate the development of and facilitate broader access to psychedelic therapies. Ibogaine, which operates via a “matrix pharmacology,” according to Columbia University professor Dalibor Sames, was a key focus of the order .
Ibogaine acts across different molecules in cells, impacting serotonin signaling via a broad transporter network rather than acting on a single target, Sames hypothesized with colleagues in a study published in January.
“What we found over and over is that ibogaine doesn’t fit into the standard pharmacological scientific paradigms,” the professor told BioSpace in June.
In late April, the FDA cleared DemeRx’s oral noribogaine candidate DMX-1001 to begin first-in-human testing. The company plans to kick off a Phase 2 trial in alcohol use disorder next year.
Alongside its potential benefit, however, ibogaine is also known for its neurotoxic and cardiotoxic effects, which can be associated with severe complications and even death. As of 2022, 33 deaths after ibogaine use had been recorded in published literature .
This latest push by HHS comes on the heels of FDA submissions for two psilocybin therapeutics, including the completion of a rolling application for Compass Pathways’ highly anticipated COMP360 for treatment-resistant depression. Compass’ announcement came just a week after a submission from competitor Usona Institute for PSIL201 in major depressive disorder.

Unplugged Performance Debuts Tesla Model Y L Suspension Packages
8 photos
Photo: Unplugged Performance
Unplugged Performance is giving Tesla Model Y L customers more ways to customize their long-wheelbase sport utility vehicles. Suspension upgrades reign supreme on this occasion, with the California-based specialist introducing no fewer than four distinct packages for the family-oriented version of the Model Y.
These suspension upgrades are joined by expanded compatibility with the company's existing wheel and brake offerings. The OEM+ Flush Fitment Kit and Perfect Flush Fitment Kit are both focused on stance and wheel positioning. The Big Three combines anti-roll hardware with lowering springs, while Core Four and Street & Trail add some well-deserved lift.
Starting with the OEM+ Flush Fitment Kit and Perfect Flush Fitment Kit, these packages use 15-millimeter (0.6 inches) wheel spacers and adjustable rear camber arms. The spacers push the wheels outward, bringing them closer to the fender edges for a meaner look, whereas the camber stuff helps the Model Y L in terms of alignment while also lowering the vehicle.
Care to guess which is the biggest difference between said packages? Springs is the right answer, indeed, with Unplugged Performance advertising mild lowering springs and moderate lowering springs, respectively. The Big Three suspension package brings together either mild or moderate lowering springs, adjustable rear camber arms, and sway bars for both ends.
Considering the aforementioned list, the Big Three also changes the cornering behavior of the Model Y L. As you're well aware, sway bars are designed to resist body roll when cornering, thus controlling how much the body leans during rapid changes of direction and through bends. Both spring options come with the very same front and rear sway bars.
Photo: Unplugged Performance The Core Four package, meanwhile, trades lowering springs for a suspension lift. Its components are sway bar end links, adjustable rear camber arms, a Luxury-spec rear sway bar, and the Leveling Lift Kit. According to Unplugged Performance, this combo should be perfect for occasional use on rural roads.
Additional clearance should also help when negotiating steep driveways. Lastly, what Unplugged Performance calls Street & Trail combines touring-oriented suspension goodies with a leveling kit.
Adjustable shocks are on the menu as well, and the off-road rear sway bar is a self-explanatory upgrade over the standard Model Y L. At $4,395 as of this writing, this package is the most expensive and comprehensive of the four.
UP has further validated three spring height options for the zero-emission sport utility vehicle. The Stock Height Dual Rate Springs retain the factory ride height. Alternatives include mild and moderate lowering springs. For maximum versatility, the stock height is recommended. Wheel choices round out this announcement, with UP offering square configurations exclusively.
For staggered fans, the UP-03 and UP-05 are forged wheels that measure 19 inches by 9.5 and 10 inches, respectively, with an ET30 offset. This arrangement allows Model Y L customers to transfer the original factory rubber directly to the Unplugged Performance wheels. A set of four wheels will set you back anything from $3,235 to $5,595 if ordered directly from Unplugged Performance.

Customized version of the LiveWire S4 Honcho displayed at EICMA 2026
Every year, the world’s largest motorcycle companies (and plenty of the world’s smallest motorcycle companies, too) converge on Milan, Italy for Europe’s premier motorcycle showcase. That means that all of the newest electric motorcycle announcements happen in one place, and we get a chance to check out the coolest developments and most interesting new gear.
Below is a list of the best things I saw while walking around the show this year, presented in no particular order.
LiveWire shows off Honcho S4 in several variants, plus new DUST Moto dirt e-bikes
LiveWire came to EICMA with perhaps its most diverse electric two-wheeler lineup yet , showing just how far the company has expanded beyond the premium electric motorcycles that originally defined the Harley-Davidson spin-off.
The new S4 Honcho family was a major focus, including the street-oriented Honcho Street, off-road Honcho Trail, and newly unveiled Honcho Skate, a stripped-down addition to the modular platform. The booth also included LiveWire’s larger S2 electric motorcycles, creating a pretty broad spectrum from lightweight urban machines up through full-size highway-capable electric motorcycles.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
A Skate variant of the Honcho shows what a stripped down mini-moto from LiveWire might look like
The other big piece of the booth was DUST Moto, which LiveWire acquired earlier this year. The production-intent DUST Hightail was displayed alongside the newly revealed DUST Spur, giving LiveWire an immediate presence in the increasingly popular lightweight electric dirt bike category.
Add in STACYC’s electric balance bikes for young riders, and the entire booth almost looked like an electric two-wheeler progression chart: start a kid on a STACYC, move up through lightweight DUST and Honcho machines, and eventually graduate to a full-size LiveWire.
GRIT motorcycles shows off three models
GR1T Motorcycles is a relatively young European electric motorcycle startup that caught my eye at EICMA with its G1 platform, a lightweight electric motorcycle designed and engineered in Italy. The basic recipe is pretty compelling: 130 km/h (81 mph) top speed, 11 kW of continuous power and 26.6 kW (36 hp) peak, all while weighing just 130 kg (287 lb).
Perhaps most importantly for urban riders, its roughly 6 kWh battery is actually split into two removable 3 kWh packs, meaning apartment dwellers can pull the batteries out and charge them inside. They’re big, but removing them is doable.
GR1T’s bikes therefore pack in around 50% more battery capacity than most electric motorcycles in this size and weight class, meaning roughly 50% more range, as well.
There are also some interesting and clever design choices, like the underslung rear suspension and the triple-camera system that includes front and rear dashcams plus a cockpit-facing camera for recording the rider.
The clever part of the overall design scheme is that GR1T isn’t developing a separate platform for every motorcycle. The same basic G1 chassis, motor, batteries, belt drive, and electronics underpin four versions: the G1S Street, G1X Scrambler, G1XR Raider, and utility-oriented G1M Mission.
Prices are set to start at €8,495 including VAT, putting these squarely in that emerging category of reasonably affordable, lightweight electric motorcycles that have enough speed for real-world commuting without chasing superbike performance.
There’s an important caveat, though: these aren’t production motorcycles yet. GR1T says it is currently fundraising , with factory development and pre-orders set to follow after funding closes and first deliveries now targeted for the first half of 2028.
So the bikes aren’t quite ready for primetime yet, but it’s definitely a company to watch.
Real Motors Project Ares
Real Motors brought one of the more visually striking electric motorcycles to EICMA with Project: ARES, a futuristic electric café racer that the American startup describes as an “Electric Analog” machine – basically an attempt to preserve the raw, mechanical connection of motorcycling while ditching unnecessary screens and gadgetry.
And there’s plenty of performance underneath the sci-fi bodywork: Real Motors lists a 75 kW (100 hp) motor, a 15 kWh battery, a 120 mph (192 km/h) top speed, and an estimated weight of 485 lb (220 kg).
The analog analogy is spot on, with the display probably the simplest and most straightforward I’ve ever seen on an electric motorcycle. There’s also no app, no subscription, and no digital handcuffs. The bike is very much the electric equivalent of a simple ICE bike that just rides, albeit with a much nicer ride.
Unlike many of the futuristic concepts scattered around EICMA, ARES is actually headed toward limited production.
Real Motors plans to build just 250 examples in its first LOT 01 production run, with pricing starting at $20,000 and North American deliveries targeted for early 2027. European deliveries are expected after homologation is completed.
The company has also brought former LiveWire CTO Vance Strader onto the project as it makes the difficult transition from a very cool prototype into an actual production motorcycle.
I actually had the chance to do a spin on the bike, and so I’ll be reporting back on the experience. But you can tell from my smile below that the ride was quite an experience!
Big thanks to CEO and Co-founder Trent Dingman for letting me borrow his helmet and the jacket off his back!
Seatylock has the most angle-grinder proof U-Lock for motorcycles
Seatylock has been my go-to e-bike lock company for several years now, and I use their locks for my several e-bikes and my wife’s e-bike too.
Now Seatylock has returned with some even more impressive locks. The company showed off its new Ultra D28 lock, which is both angle grinder-proof and wide enough to lock the wheel of a motorcycle. It solves the problem of how do you make a lock strong enough for a motorcycle but also small and light enough that you can actually carry it with you, unlike a massive chain lock that usually stays where you park your motorcycle overnight.
In the image below, you can see the shackle next to an exposed section demonstrating the diamond coating that essentially destroys angle grinder discs – even diamond coated discs.
Multiple sizes offer protection for motorcycle and bicycle wheels, plus there’s a ground anchor with the same angle grinder-proof material
The company also has a slightly smaller version of the same lock designed for bicycles.
Both will absolutely destroy even the toughest angle grinder discs. Sure, eventually someone could cut through them, but it may take a dozen discs and by that point the thief has moved on to an easier target.
Flying Flea
At EICMA 2026, Royal Enfield continued expanding its electric motorcycle ambitions with its Flying Flea sub-brand , showcasing the scrambler-style motorcycle alongside its growing lineup of lightweight, retro-inspired electric motorcycles.
There were several interesting colorways and customized designs on display, showcasing the Flying Flea’s stylish design.
The new models blend Royal Enfield’s classic design heritage with modern electric technology, targeting urban riders and those looking for a fun, approachable electric motorcycle rather than a high-performance machine.
With distinctive styling, compact proportions, and an emphasis on accessible riding, the Flying Flea lineup represents Royal Enfield’s effort to carve out a place in the emerging market for smaller electric motorcycles while maintaining the character that has made its gasoline-powered bikes so popular.
Yamaha NMAX E
Yamaha showed off its new NMAX E electric scooter , bringing battery-powered performance to one of the brand’s most recognizable urban scooter families.
Designed as an electric alternative to the popular gasoline-powered NMAX, the new model combines familiar sporty styling with a quiet, low-maintenance electric drivetrain aimed at everyday city commuting.
The NMAX E uses Yamaha’s new compact eAxle powertrain, shared with the larger-wheeled XENTER E, and delivers up to 7.5 kW (10 hp) of peak power, putting it in the 125cc-equivalent class.
With its practical step-through design, automatic operation, and approachable performance, the NMAX E represents another step in Yamaha’s push to electrify its urban mobility lineup, particularly in European markets where scooters are already a popular alternative to cars.
Segway safety scooters
Segway showed off a new vision for safer electric scooters, including its futuristic X Cruiser concept that takes rider protection to a whole new level.
Rather than relying solely on traditional motorcycle safety equipment, the X Cruiser explores automotive-inspired features such as integrated seats with seatbelts, partial enclosures, and even a fully roofed version designed to offer additional protection from the elements.
The concept includes several configurations, ranging from a more conventional open scooter to a partially enclosed design and a fully covered model that looks like a cross between a motorcycle and a tiny electric car. While these designs are still concepts rather than production-ready scooters, they demonstrate how Segway is rethinking two-wheeled transportation by exploring ways to make electric scooters safer, more comfortable, and potentially more appealing to riders who might otherwise be hesitant to trade four wheels for two.
Eli Zero gets even faster – and more racecar-like!
Eli Electric Vehicles took to EICMA 2026 to display its compact Eli Zero electric quadricycle, a tiny two-seat urban EV designed to offer much of the convenience of a car without the size, weight, or expense of a conventional automobile.
With its enclosed cabin, side-by-side seating, and ultra-compact footprint, the Eli Zero offers a practical alternative to larger vehicles for short city trips, combining the weather protection and comfort of a car with the maneuverability and efficiency of a much smaller vehicle.
The company revealed a more powerful L7e-class version of the Eli Zero that it had previously teased, expanding the vehicle’s capabilities beyond its existing L6e configuration. The new Race Edition also pushes the envelope farther with custom interior and a few extra accents to the body.
With growing interest in smaller, more efficient urban transportation, Eli’s presence at EICMA definitely underlined how the show is increasingly embracing electric mobility solutions that go beyond traditional motorcycles and scooters.
NIU e-scooters get MY27 updates
NIU showed off its latest lineup of electric scooters, continuing the brand’s push to make battery-powered two-wheelers a practical alternative to gasoline-powered urban transportation. Known for its sleek designs, connected technology, and approachable electric scooters, NIU highlighted models aimed at a range of riders, from everyday city commuters to those looking for more powerful machines capable of keeping up with faster urban traffic.
The company showed off several new models for the 2027 model year, with scooters that combine modern styling with features such as smartphone connectivity, smart security systems, and efficient electric drivetrains, all while maintaining the simplicity and low operating costs that make electric scooters so appealing.
While I didn’t see anything groundbreaking at the brand’s booth this year, the incremental updates look to push new tech features further throughout the brand’s many models, helping more of NIU’s offerings enter that premium level that the company has been known for.
Honda EV Outlier is extra futuristic
For something a bit wilder, Honda shared its futuristic EV Outlier Concept , an electric motorcycle that explores what two-wheeled design could look like when engineers are freed from the constraints of traditional gasoline-powered motorcycles.
With its long, low-slung profile, radically different riding position, and futuristic bodywork, the EV Outlier looks more like something out of a science fiction movie than a conventional motorcycle. The concept features electric motors integrated into both wheels, giving it two-wheel drive while opening up new possibilities for packaging and weight distribution.
Rather than simply replacing a combustion engine with a battery and motor, Honda used the EV Outlier to rethink the entire motorcycle layout, demonstrating how electrification could lead to entirely new types of riding experiences.
While the bike remains a design concept with no announced production plans, it offers an intriguing glimpse into Honda’s vision for the future of electric motorcycles.
Vespa Elettrica is getting removable batteries
Vespa showed off its next-generation electric scooter lineup at EICMA, including electric versions of the Primavera, Sprint S, and Primavera Tech. While they don’t look radically different, there’s a lot more happening underneath the familiar steel bodywork.
A new Italian-made, rare-earth-free electric motor improves efficiency and performance, while the 45 km/h Primavera and Sprint S now feature removable batteries.
The faster 67 km/h Primavera Tech gets up to 90 km of WMTC range – a 12.5% improvement – along with an updated vehicle management system and more efficient charger.

The streamlined operation has allowed the company to better connect global markets through its Ontario hub, resulting in increased demand from shippers attracted to more route options. In addition to more flights, non-domestic activity benefitted from favorable market conditions that have raised yields across the air cargo industry, where capacity has not kept up with the 6% volume growth year-to-date.
The all-cargo carrier late Wednesday reported revenue of US$201.4 million, a 30.3% increase year over year. Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization grew 28% to $63.4 million, as stronger charter and long-term contracted flying activity more than offset higher maintenance, ground and pilot costs. Both figures were the highest ever during the July-to-September period.
Management said improved aircraft utilization, reflected by a 13.3% increase in block hours per aircraft, played an important role in profit margins increasing 31.5% over the prior-year quarter.
Cargojet ( TSX: CJT ) this year implemented a revamped business model called One Fleet, One Network aimed at improving efficiency and expanding its global reach by centrally managing aircraft, network capacity and commercial sales for domestic express, long-term dedicated contract flying, and charter operations rather than treating them as independent business lines.
“This integrated approach allows us to match capacity more effectively with customer demand, improve aircraft productivity, and pursue opportunities that generate the greatest value across our networks. Our focus is on generating higher-quality revenue, maximizing the productivity of our existing assets, and translating that performance into stronger earnings and free cash flow,” said CEO Pauline Dhillon during an earnings conference call with analysts.
“By connecting our domestic network with key international markets, we can create new cargo flows, increase network density, and generate incremental revenue from our existing infrastructure and aircraft,” she added. A big focus is on repurposing aircraft when they are not operating in the domestic overnight network or on dedicated customer routes.
Why It Matters: Cargojet is a mid-tier cargo carrier that serves logistics giants like Amazon, DHL and UPS.
The network restructuring shares commonalities with FedEx, which is in the process of melding separate ground and express networks into a more cohesive, and less expensive to run, whole.
More charter options
Cargojet’s strategy took another step forward with the announcement that it will expand scheduled freighter service to three times per week between its base in Hamilton, Ontario — about 40 miles southwest of Toronto — and Miami, effective Dec. 2. The extra frequency provides greater connectivity between Europe, Asia, Canada and key destinations in South America, giving freight forwarders more shipping options and flexibility, according to the company.
Dhillon said the carrier has already secured volume commitments from existing customers ahead of the Miami launch.
Changes to the charter business are also paying dividends, she said, as the carrier evolves from primarily offering ad hoc flying toward a more balanced mix of scheduled service and customer-specific rentals. Revenue for all-in charters, under which a customer pays a fixed amount per flight that covers all costs, was up 88%.
“This evolution provides greater revenue visibility, creates opportunities to build consistent cargo volumes, and allows us to deploy available aircraft capacity more productively,” the CEO said.
The charter business benefitted from the mid-September addition of a second weekly frequency between Hamilton and Liège, Belgium, because of increased demand. The service is operated by a Boeing 767 converted freighter, which continues onward to Tel Aviv, Israel. And it began flying weekend charter flights to China.
Cargojet operates a mix of 42 leased and owned Boeing 767 medium widebody converted freighters and Boeing 757 large narrowbody freighters, one more than last year.
The carrier has been flying several freighters on behalf of UPS, which retired its fleet of 27 large MD-11 cargo jets following the deadly crash of one of its planes last November. As UPS continues to take delivery of factory-built 767 freighters from Boeing the need for outside capacity goes down and Dhillon said most UPS work will end this quarter.
The loss in UPS business will largely be offset by new contractual flying to South America, which has already begun, as well as additional flying opportunities to China and the Far East that are currently being negotiated.
Management stated that it is increasingly focused on revenue quality and is willing to reprice contracts when they become eligible for adjustment, saying the company’s high on-time performance and overall service justify premium pricing.
October domestic volumes were strong and customer shipping forecasts suggest that the current peak season should compare favorably with last year. International flying this year for customers like DHL Express has also been strong as geopolitical disruptions have led businesses to divert some cargo to air transport.
Cargojet’s new pilot contract , which calls for a 53% increase in pay over four years, took effect during the third quarter. The company previously said it would pass those cost increases onto customers.

The Port of Los Angeles recorded its busiest October ever, handling 1,026,872 twenty-foot equivalent units, or TEUs, and surpassing 1 million TEUs for the second consecutive month for the first time in its history.
October’s total was the second-highest monthly volume ever at the nation’s busiest container port, following September’s all-time record. The port has now reached the million-TEU threshold three times in 2026, another first. According to the port, no other U.S. port has handled 1 million TEUs in a single month.
From June through October, Los Angeles processed nearly 5 million TEUs, its strongest five-month stretch on record.
“What’s remarkable isn’t just the record volume but our ability to sustain this level of activity month after month,” Port of Los Angeles Executive Director Gene Seroka said in a media briefing. “It’s a testament to the strength of our supply chain partners and the tremendous work being done across our waterfront every day.”
Loaded imports reached approximately 538,620 TEUs in October, up 25% from a year earlier and 30% above the port’s five-year October average. Loaded exports fell 7% from October 2025 to 114,981 TEUs.
The port also handled 373,271 empty TEUs, setting a monthly record for the second consecutive month as ocean carriers repositioned containers to Asia for additional shipments.
Seroka attributed the elevated cargo activity to continued consumer spending, retailers replenishing inventories, changes in trade policy and ongoing challenges along other global shipping routes.
“Our customers are choosing Los Angeles for the speed, reliability and reach of our supply chain,” Seroka said. “These past five months have demonstrated what we can accomplish while moving extraordinary volumes of cargo efficiently to destinations across America.”
Through the first 10 months of 2026, the port processed approximately 9,108,497 TEUs, up 5% from the same period last year and 9% above its five-year average.
Record box volumes have made dwell a stubborn issue as Los Angeles has 39.8% of its import boxes wait nine or more days for an on-dock intermodal train, according to monitor The Dwell. Four days is considered normal. That compares to 30.2% at the neighboring Port of Long Beach. Most of those containers are bound for BNSF (NYSE: BRK-B ), the monitor said.
Why it matters : The record figures show an uneven trade picture, as loaded imports rose sharply while loaded exports declined, and empty-container repositioning contributed substantially to overall activity.

VTOL Drone Burns Jet Fuel to Charge Batteries and Fly for 1,300 Miles
6 photos
Photo: Skyways
There are so many new and relatively new companies in the business of making drones in one form or another that it is almost impossible to keep track of them all. Luckily, from time to time, some of these businesses come into the spotlight with something fresh, exciting, or otherwise remarkable. Like, say, a new vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) cargo aircraft that will commence operations by the end of the year.
The crew behind this design is Texas -based Skyways, a company that has been around for about a decade or so to develop autonomous aviation solutions. It has tried to do so with something called the V2, but that's not what we're here to discuss. That would be something called the Skyreach.
Presented this week as a long-range Group 3 autonomous VTOL meant to carry cargo, the aircraft is getting ready to enter service in the hands of undisclosed defense and commercial customers as soon as next month.
The drone has a lot of things going for it, as most other drones do, but it is one capability that stands out the most: range. That would be a highly impressive 1,300 miles (2,092 km) of travel one way and a total flight time of 18 hours, with some footnotes.
The Skyreach can fly that far thanks to the dual hybrid system that powers it. It combines a series of batteries to power its eight electric motors, and a heavy-fuel engine (which can burn JP-5 and Jet A-1 fuels) that is used, aside from cruising, to recharge the batteries in flight. This eliminates the need to recharge or swap batteries.
The hybrid system can get the drone to its maximum distance when carrying only ten pounds (4.5 kg) of stuff and the maximum fuel load – the thing can only fly while carrying 100 pounds (45 kg) of combined fuel and payload – and, naturally, that drops when more weight is added.
Another thing that makes the design special is the configurable payload bay, which can be specced so that cargo of different shapes, sizes, and uses, including temperature-controlled items, can be loaded and transported. Then, the design can fly in winds as powerful as 40 knots and in temperatures ranging from minus 5 degrees Fahrenheit to 120 degrees (minus 20 degrees Celsius to 49 degrees).
Skyways said the drone can be flown at a high frequency, and as most other VTOLs out there, it does not need runways to take off and land. On top of that, we're also told it costs one-tenth the price of a helicopter, but, to be fair, helicopters are a lot more capable than this.
As said, the Skyreach is expected to fly operationally as soon as December 2026. It's unclear how many of them are in the hands of customers, but Skyways revealed that it plans to have some 1,000 of them in the skies over the next five years, serving both commercial and defense needs.

By: Northern Miner Staff November 13, 2026
Freeport-McMoRan (NYSE: FCX) has agreed to pay $110 million (US$77.2 million) for a controlling stake in TDG Gold’s (TSXV: TDG) Aurora West project in British Columbia, advancing consolidation around the neighbouring Aurora copper-gold discovery held by Freeport and Amarc Resources (TSXV: AHR).
The initial purchase covers 51% of two companies that will hold the property, TDG said Thursday . Freeport can lift its stake by funding $80 million in exploration and paying TDG another $40 million.
“Our retained interest in the Aurora West Property through the joint venture also gives our shareholders continued exposure to its upside potential,” TDG CEO Fletcher Morgan said.
Proceeds from the deal will strengthen TDG’s cash holdings without issuing shares and help it advance its Shasta gold-silver project, Morgan said.
Toodoggone partnership
The transaction could bring adjoining ground into the Freeport-Amarc partnership in the Toodoggone district. Amarc has rights to participate in acquisitions that fall wholly or partly within 2 km of the partnership’s property.
TDG shares dropped 7% to 66¢ Friday morning in Toronto, valuing the company at about $186 million. They’ve traded between 39.5¢ and $1.11 over the past year.
Freeport’s options would raise its stake to 75% in Aurora West JVCo and 100% in ClaimsCo, which holds two specified claims. TDG would retain 25% of the former and a 2% net smelter return royalty over the latter’s claims. Shasta and the Baker property are excluded from the sale.
TDG won’t have to contribute to either company during the earn-in option period. If Freeport doesn’t exercize the option, it would retain 51%, with subsequent costs shared in proportion to ownership, subject to dilution.
Freeport has committed to spend $30 million of the $80 million exploration total within three years of closing, including at least $15 million in the first two, TDG said. Completion requires TSX Venture Exchange approval. TDG expects the pre-closing reorganization in December, with closing five business days after conditions are satisfied or waived.
Participation rights
Claims and other rights acquired wholly or partly within the area of common interest must be offered at cost to Aurora Minerals, the existing Freeport-Amarc joint venture, Amarc said in a separate announcement Thursday. TDG’s Aurora West drilling has focused on ground within that area, it said.
Freeport owns 60% of Aurora Minerals and is earning another 10% by funding $75 million of staged spending. About $40 million to $45 million has already been spent. Amarc says Freeport must fund the first estimated $30 million to $35 million of applicable acquisition costs through the remaining earn-in expenditures.
After Freeport reaches 70%, Amarc would fund its 30% share of applicable costs. Amarc awaits formal notice and would then have at least 45 days to elect to participate. It raised $20 million in September and has appointed Agentis Capital Mining Partners as financial adviser.
Amarc separately announced completion of a $22-million exploration program at the 630-sq.-km Joy district. Freeport funded almost 14,000 metres of drilling in 16 holes, testing Aurora and other targets. Assays remain pending.
The district is connected to Prince George by highways and resource roads serving the Kemess area. A 230-kilovolt transmission line runs alongside the resource road to the former Kemess South mine, according to Amarc’s project overview. Spare capacity may be available to other projects, the company says.

source_document.body:
UPS has sued the federal government to recover tariffs the Supreme Court struck down in February. Much of the money would go to customers who paid the duties.
What’s Related
UPS is asking the U.S. Court of International Trade to order U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) to reopen certain import entries and refund the duties, with interest. The tariffs were imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA), and the Supreme Court ruled on Feb. 20 that the law didn’t give the president the power to impose them.
The case covers import entries for which Customs had already made a final decision on the duties owed, including entries subject to a protest. UPS was the importer of record on those entries, meaning it was the party responsible for the goods when they cleared Customs.
Why UPS needs a judge
CBP has been paying refunds in phases through its online system, known as CAPE. The first phase opened April 20 and covered entries Customs hadn’t finalized yet, plus some it had closed only recently.
On Oct. 6, CBP opened a third phase for entries where the duties were already final. There’s a catch, though. Those entries qualify only if the importer has a case at the Court of International Trade and a court order telling Customs to reopen them. UPS is asking for that order.
RELATED: Why Retailers Are Losing So Much Money on Returns
Breaking down UPS' payments to customers
UPS received about $500 million in the first refund round. By Sept. 30, it had passed about $230 million along to customers and still had about $270 million to distribute, based on figures in its third-quarter filing.
UPS says its customers paid the tariffs in many cases. Customs sends the refund to UPS as importer of record, and UPS matches each entry to the original payment before passing the money along. It plans to do the same with whatever it recovers through the lawsuit.
How customers get paid
For first-phase refunds, UPS first applies the refund and any applicable interest to past-due invoices on the account. It then sends any remaining balance to the customer.
Shippers can see which of their shipments qualify using UPS’s online refund lookup tool. You can log in to see everything tied to your account, or search by tracking number or delivery address. The tool shows each shipment’s refund phase, status and amount. Entries marked “future phase” could be part of a later CBP refund round.

An Army official identified Lt. Col. Brandon Carroll Tyner as the U.S. soldier arrested earlier this week in the United Kingdom for reportedly assisting Russian intelligence in what FBI Director Kash Patel described as “allegations of espionage.”
Tyner, 41, began serving in the Army as a human resources officer — military occupational specialty 42H — in January 2008, the official told Military Times. Tyner’s deployments included tours in Afghanistan, Qatar and Iraq.
At the time of his arrest, he was assigned to Imjin Barracks , a British Army base near Gloucestershire, England, which hosts NATO’s Allied Rapid Reaction Corps. His arrest came shortly after the U.S. removed aircraft from British military bases over an unrelated reported threat from Iran.
Tyner was arrested under Sections 1 and 3 of Britain’s 2023 National Security Act and the Army said officials were investigating two locations in Gloucestershire. Counter Terrorism Policing London is leading the investigation and the accused officer remains in custody at a London police station.
“This important arrest involves allegations of espionage, which is of the utmost concern to the United States and our allies,” Patel said in a statement, adding that the FBI had made 167 counterintelligence and espionage arrests over the last 21 months.
Brig. Gen. Sean Stinchon, the commanding general of U.S. Army Counterintelligence Command, thanked the FBI authorities in the UK and encouraged anyone who notices something suspicious to consult officials.
“The alleged conduct of a senior soldier, entrusted with sensitive information, is a sobering reminder that insider threats are real and persistent. I encourage anyone who thinks they’ve witnessed something suspicious to report it to their local counterintelligence office,” he said in a statement.
The arrest comes amid U.S. European Command’s “See Something, Do Something” campaign , which calls on troops, family members and civilian employees to be vigilant about their digital presence and report unusual behavior to authorities. Though the campaign did not identify a specific threat, experts have warned that Russia is ramping up its hybrid warfare.
The Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project, known as ACLED, said in an October report that Russia had increased its hybrid threats across Europe — such as targeting aviation in Germany, attempting to sabotage critical infrastructure in Poland and ramping up drone incursions in Romania and Moldova — in an attempt to weaken the region’s support for Ukraine. The report expects those threats to grow, noting that Moscow would likely use cyberattacks and ramp up attacks against defense and transportation infrastructure.

Posted By: FREDERIC TOMESCO November 13, 2026
Capstone Copper (TSX: CS; ASX: CSC) has lowered the bottom of its annual copper production forecast by 5,000 tonnes after delaying the full restart of its Pinto Valley operation in Arizona until mid-December.
The primary crusher needs additional repairs to major mechanical components being manufactured off-site by the original equipment maker, the company said Thursday in an update . Mobile crushers should allow partial processing to resume in mid-November.
While the 5,000-tonne impact is “modest,” it “adds to a difficult operational year at Pinto Valley and [the company’s] Mantoverde” operation in Chile, Jefferies mining analyst Tariq Fahad said Thursday in a note. “In our view, the bigger concern is execution, with investors likely looking for improved operating reliability into 2027.”
Capstone shares dropped 4.5% to C$10.26 late Friday morning in Toronto, extending Thursday’s 6.5% decline. The company’s market capitalization now stands at about $7.9 billion (US$5.6 billion).
Additional pressure
The setback puts more pressure on a year-end recovery that Capstone was already counting on. In its Oct. 29 results, the company forecast annual production at the bottom of its 200,000-to-230,000-tonne range, with cash costs at the upper end of guidance.
The revised production floor is 195,000 tonnes. Capstone estimated the additional downtime would reduce this year’s copper output by about 5,000 tonnes, depending on restart timing. Temporary mobile crushers could support throughput of up to 40,000 tonnes daily during the interim restart.
That would be about two-thirds of Pinto Valley’s nominal milling capacity. The open-pit operation, about 130 km east of Phoenix, has a 60,000-tonne-per-day concentrator and produces copper and molybdenum concentrates as well as copper cathode.
Supply risk
Capstone is also grappling with the effects of a national strike in Chile. Called by Chilean trucking groups and a civic movement to protest high fuel prices, the stoppage threatens concentrate and cathode shipments and deliveries of fuel and sulphuric acid, Capstone said Thursday.
Preventive measures and on-site storage have so far protected output at Capstone’s two Chilean operations, the company added. Sulphuric acid is used to leach copper from ore, while fuel powers mining equipment.
Together with the delays at Pinto Valley, the Chilean truckers’ strike introduces “incremental downside risk to year-end production,” TD Securities mining analyst Craig Hutchison said in a note.
At National Bank Financial, mining analyst Shane Nagle cut his rating on Capstone to sector perform from outperform, citing the “near-term operational uncertainty.”
Consistent operational performance at Mantoverde and Pinto Valley “will be important to supporting a re-rating which has been materially impacted by [Thursday’s] release,” he said.
Higher grades
Pinto Valley produced 6,358 tonnes of copper in the third quarter, compared with 9,949 tonnes a year earlier. Its nine-month output was 27,115 tonnes, down from 30,960 tonnes, Capstone reported in October.
The plant had restarted with mobile crushers on Oct. 1 before primary crusher commissioning began Oct. 21. Additional repairs were then identified.
Capstone was looking to higher grades at Mantoverde and Mantos Blancos, alongside completion of the Mantoverde concentrator expansion tie-in, to lift fourth-quarter production. Group output totalled 45,218 tonnes in the third quarter, down 18% from a year earlier.
The company agreed in September to sell its Cozamin mine in Mexico to Luca Mining (TSXV: LUCA) for up to $385 million (C$549 million). Closing was expected in the fourth quarter, subject to conditions and approvals, Capstone said in October. The sale would add financial flexibility for the company’s growth projects.
Capstone’s annual production target includes a full year of Cozamin output.
