Australia's 2027 Chery Stockman Plug-In Hybrid Pickup Truck Priced From AUD 52,990
12 photos
Photo: Chery
Chinese automaker Chery has released Australian-market pricing information for its plug-in hybrid pickup truck. Gifted with a four-pot diesel, the Stockman is now available in two specifications. AUD 52,990 gets you the lesser grade, whereas the Ultimate will set prospective customers back AUD 57,990 at the very least.
Unique in the segment due to its diesel engine, this fellow competes against the plug-in hybrid gasoline-fueled GWM Cannon and BYD Shark 6. Its 2.5-liter turbo diesel plug-in hybrid setup is listed up to 350 kilowatts (469 horsepower) and 800 Newton-meters (590 pound-feet) of twist, numbers that should appeal to a plethora of buyers.
Priced below the BYD yet pricier than the GWM, the Chery produces a respectable 140 kW (188 hp) and 450 Nm (332 lb-ft) without any kind of electrified assistance. A four-speed hybrid tranny handles power delivery, whereas a 34-kWh battery of the lithium-iron-phosphate variety enables full-electric driving.
Chery advertises up to 100 kilometers (62 miles) of electric-only range on the NEDC test cycle, which is curious when you remember that NEDC is very old news. The high-voltage battery supports DC fast charging at up to 70 kilowatts and AC charging at no more than 6.6 kilowatts.
In addition to the under-tub LFP battery, customers also get an 80-liter fuel tank. On the combined test cycle, it should consume anything between 1.0 and 1.1 liters of diesel per 100 kilometers while emitting 25 to 30 grams of CO2 per kilometer. All in all, not bad at all. Both grades of the diesel-fueled Stockman employ four-wheel drive.
Photo: Chery Center and rear diff locks are standard on the base Urban spec. Equipped with leaf springs out back and double wishbones for the front axle, the Stockman rides on 18-inch wheels and provides up to 235 millimeters (9.3 inches) of ground clearance. A dual cab that measures 3,250 millimeters (128 inches) between its axles, the Chinese newcomer is up there with the segment's bests in terms of towing capacity.
Chery advertises 3,495 kilograms (7,705 pounds) braked and 750 kilograms (1,653 pounds) unbraked. The maximum payload rating of 810 kilograms (1,786 pounds) only applies to the Urban trim level. Opting for the Ultimate gets you more standard kit, including a front differential lock, 14 audio speakers, and a head-up display.
AUD 5,000 pricier, the Ultimate further sweetens the deal with a digital rearview mirror, a heated steering wheel, plus heating and ventilation for the front seats. In the Australian market, customer deliveries are scheduled to start in February 2027. That gives Aussie buyers a few short months to decide whether the diesel-electric combo makes more sense than current gasoline-electric alternatives or a purely diesel pickup.
Going forward, Chery 's Australian subsidiary plans to introduce a gasoline plug-in hybrid. Due in the second half of 2027, presumably as a 2028 model, the second powertrain is estimated to generate a frankly ridiculous 395 kilowatts (530 horsepower) and 1,000 Newton-meters (738 pound-feet).

NeoVolta, a U.S.-based energy technology company delivering scalable energy storage solutions, said its majority-owned subsidiary, NeoVolta Power, has entered into a $116-million master purchase agreement with a leading energy solutions provider.
Under the agreement announced November 13, NeoVolta Power will supply FEOC-compliant battery energy storage systems (BESS), with product deliveries scheduled for 2027. The agreement establishes a substantial base of contracted business, providing increased visibility into NeoVolta’s near-term manufacturing activity and supporting the company’s continued commercial expansion.
The purchase orders would provide a substantial foundation for NeoVolta’s manufacturing ramp in Pendergrass, Georgia, supporting increased production volumes as the company expands its domestic energy storage operations. As demand for FEOC-compliant domestic supply chains continue to grow, NeoVolta believes its U.S. manufacturing capabilities position the company to play an increasingly important role in the rapidly expanding energy storage market.
“Securing this $116-million agreement represents a major milestone for NeoVolta, and we believe this is only the beginning of a much larger growth trajectory for our company,” said Ardes Johnson, CEO of NeoVolta. “As we scale production in Georgia and fulfill these commitments, we are building the foundation for rapid, sustained growth while positioning NeoVolta to meet the accelerating demand for domestically manufactured battery energy storage systems and become one of the leading U.S. suppliers in the industry.”
NeoVolta is an innovator in energy storage solutions dedicated to advancing reliable, high-performance power infrastructure for residential, commercial, and utility applications. With a focus on scalable technology, domestic manufacturing, and strategic partnerships, NeoVolta is positioned to support the accelerating transition toward resilient energy systems.
—This content was contributed by the communications team for NeoVolta .

Carlos Victor Mestanza Cercado acknowledged participating in the $100 million Brink’s jewelry heist in a newly filed federal plea agreement. The Nov. 9 filing details how conspirators followed a semitruck approximately 300 miles before stealing its cargo. The group broke trailer locks and removed 24 bags containing valuable merchandise. Mestanza also admitted involvement in several earlier electronics thefts targeting commercial shipments across Southern California .
The theft occurred July 11, 2022, after a jewelry exhibition in San Mateo, California. Federal court records show the Brink’s vehicle carried 73 bags of merchandise from the international event. Conspirators tracked the shipment through multiple locations before reaching Lebec, north of Los Angeles. The theft followed several days of surveillance targeting high-value freight leaving the exhibition.
Mestanza signed the agreement Nov. 4, and federal prosecutors finalized the document five days later. He agreed to plead guilty to one count of interference with commerce by robbery. That charge concerns a separate March 2022 robbery involving Apple AirTags, rather than the Brink’s shipment. Prosecutors agreed to seek dismissal of his remaining charges at sentencing.
How thieves tracked the Brink’s shipment
The operation began before the truck departed San Mateo, according to the agreed statement of facts. A conspirator scouted the international jewelry show July 8, 9 and 10, 2022. That individual communicated with Mestanza and other participants about stealing merchandise after the exhibition. By July 10, the group had focused its attention on the Brink’s semitruck.
During the overnight hours, participants coordinated their movements through telephone communications. They followed the commercial vehicle from San Mateo toward Buttonwillow and Lebec in Kern County. The indictment also describes conspirators serving as lookouts while accomplices entered targeted trucks. Conspirators eventually breached the trailer’s locks and escaped with the jewelry.
The thieves transported the stolen jewelry to East Hollywood after leaving Lebec. Participants later deactivated cellphone numbers they had used during the operation. Federal court records identify that action as an attempt to conceal their identities. Those communications form part of Mestanza’s admissions concerning the July 2022 theft.
Earlier cargo thefts reveal coordinated tactics
The agreement also describes three earlier incidents involving Samsung electronics and Apple tracking devices. On March 2, 2022, conspirators followed a commercial truck carrying Samsung products through Ontario, California. When its driver stopped at a 7-Eleven, participants approached with a fabricated request for translation assistance. Others removed electronics while the distraction continued, causing losses victims valued at approximately $240,573.
Nine days later, the group targeted a box truck transporting Apple AirTags from China to a Fontana warehouse. Participants monitored the driver during a restaurant stop before attempting to remove merchandise. Mestanza drove the van intended to carry the stolen products, according to his admissions. When the driver discovered the theft, a conspirator confronted him while holding a small knife. The indictment quotes the threat: “Don’t move, or I will f____ you up!”
The victim feared for his safety and declined to intervene. Conspirators escaped with approximately $57,377 in Apple AirTags, according to the agreement. Mestanza also maintained an 87-minute telephone conversation with another participant to coordinate information about the driver’s movements.
On May 25, 2022, participants approached a semitruck at a Pilot Flying J location in Fontana. One conspirator used a crowbar to force entry before the group fled. Later that day, they targeted another commercial vehicle awaiting unloading elsewhere in the city. The thieves removed Samsung electronics worth about $14,000 after cutting plastic surrounding the boxes.
Plea agreement raises $100 million restitution dispute
Mestanza faces a maximum sentence of 20 years in federal prison under the proposed guilty plea. Prosecutors have agreed to seek dismissal of his remaining indictment counts at sentencing. The court may still consider conduct underlying those charges when determining punishment. A change-of-plea hearing is scheduled for Nov. 19 before U.S. District Judge Kenly Kiya Kato.
The agreement identifies a substantial disagreement over restitution connected to the stolen jewelry. Prosecutors currently estimate the applicable amount at no less than $100,312,031.54. Mestanza’s defense contends certain victims declared less than $10 million under their Brink’s transportation contracts. Federal attorneys dispute whether those declarations limit restitution for the actual losses.
The valuation dispute dates to August 2022, when Brink’s sued affected jewelers in federal court . The company identified $8.7 million in combined declared shipment values and sought to limit its contractual liability. Jewelers maintained that their stolen merchandise carried substantially higher values and challenged the company’s responsibility for the losses. The dispute highlights differences between declared cargo values, claimed merchandise losses and potential criminal restitution.
The defendant also acknowledged actions following the public announcement of his indictment in June 2025. He searched online for information about wanted individuals, Interpol and international travel routes. Investigators documented messages concerning a major robbery and crossing the U.S.-Mexico border. Authorities detained Mestanza July 1, 2025, during a Panama City airport layover between Guatemala and Ecuador.
The June 2025 federal indictment charged seven defendants in the cargo theft operation. Three others, Jazael Padilla Resto, Pablo Raul Lugo Larroig and Jorge Enrique Alban, face trial in March 2027. Authorities continue seeking Victor Hugo Valencia Solorzano and Eduardo Macias Ibarra, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office. Immigration officials deported Jeson Nelon Presilla Flores to Ecuador in December 2025, although prosecutors still seek his trial.
Federal authorities recovered some stolen jewelry during searches in June 2025. However, the plea agreement does not establish the total value of recovered merchandise. The final restitution amount and potential prison sentence also remain unresolved. Mestanza must still appear before the court to formally enter his guilty plea.
Why it matters
The Brink’s theft highlights the financial exposure created when declared cargo values differ significantly from claimed merchandise losses. Brokers, carriers and shippers must understand contractual liability limits while strengthening shipment security and driver verification procedures.

The UK will buy three counter-mine "motherships" from Norway under a new agreement. (UK Ministry of Defence)
MILAN — The UK this week formalized plans to purchase three new mine-hunting “motherships” that can deploy unmanned mine countermeasure assets, as part of a defense cooperation agreement with Norway.
Under the UK-Norway Lunna House Agreement , signed last December, the British government announced its intention to join the Norwegian P1118 Standardized Vessel Program to develop offshore support vessels as motherships for autonomous mine-hunting systems.
The decision, for which £90 million ($119.1 million) has been allocated, was formalized on Thursday by British Defense Secretary Wes Streeting and his Norwegian counterpart, Tore O. Sandvik, at the Atlantic Future Forum in Oslo.
“This deal strengthens our ability to protect freedom of navigation, which is critical to our security and our economy …[We are] using the biggest sustained increase in defense spending since the Cold War to put the latest modern technology in the hands of our sailors,” Streeting said.
The British Ministry of Defense said the vessels, built on the same family as Norway’s naval version of the P1118 design, will help keep sailors “further from danger” and, as a result, support “anti-submarine warfare capabilities on NATO’s northern flank.”
The first ship is expected to arrive in 2031, and the deal includes an option for London to order three more.
The threat posed by naval mines, especially in the Strait of Hormuz, has surged since the start of the Iran war in February, when Tehran launched mine-laying operations to restrict navigation of the waterway. In Thursday’s announcement, the British MoD called these operations “illegal.” It said they caused “major disruption to the global trade in energy,” adding that the new mine-hunting capabilities will help the UK stay ahead of this threat.

Evergreen Marine reported after-tax net profit of $2.16 billion for the first nine months of 2026, up 18.13% from a year earlier, as a strong third quarter boosted the Taiwanese container carrier’s earnings.
The world’s seventh-largest liner said consolidated revenue for January through September rose 15.36% to $10.29 billion. Earnings per share reached approximately $1.00, surpassing the approximately $0.96 recorded for all of 2025.
The Taiwan company’s ( 2603.TW ) third-quarter after-tax net profit surged 114.36% year over year to $1.42 billion, while consolidated revenue increased 51.44% to $4.46 billion. Quarterly earnings per share reached approximately $.65, an eight-quarter high.
Third-quarter profit increased by approximately $756.1 million from a year earlier. The quarterly net profit margin reached 31.76%, compared with 20.96% for the first nine months, reflecting stronger peak-season freight rates and improved load factors.
Container shipping demand that began strengthening in the second quarter continued into the third, sustaining peak-season momentum throughout the period.
At the same time, unresolved geopolitical disruptions and congestion at major global hub ports reduced effective shipping capacity. That tighter supply-demand balance supported higher revenue and profit, while stronger utilization of available vessel space helped improve margins.
Why it matters: Evergreen’s nine-month results demonstrate the earnings impact of a strong peak season: third-quarter profit more than doubled, helping the company exceed its full-year 2025 earnings per share in just nine months.
